# @noisedlabs/sdk

<!-- repo-config:badges:start (generated by scripts/release/apply-repo-config.mjs from scripts/release/repo-config.json; do not edit by hand) -->
[![npm @noisedlabs/sdk](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@noisedlabs/sdk.svg?label=%40noisedlabs%2Fsdk)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@noisedlabs/sdk) [![CI](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/LICENSE)
<!-- repo-config:badges:end -->

TypeScript SDK for **Noised, the quantum security layer for Solana** ([noised.fun](https://noised.fun)).

Noised has four parts, and this SDK covers all of them:

- **Launch**: tokens nobody can rug, not even their creator. One program holds every privileged role itself, opens trading with a fair pro-rata batch, goes live only with its creator's post-quantum signature, and leaves an on-chain certificate.
- **Vault**: post-quantum custody (LM-OTS one-time keys) for any token.
- **Shield**: private balances (Token-2022 confidential transfers) for any token.
- **Verify**: anyone can re-check a token against **QSL-1**, the open standard the layer defines ([QSL-1](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/standard/QSL-1.md)), from live accounts only.

With this SDK you can check any mint against QSL-1 and show the result as a plain-English badge, read and independently re-verify Noised launches, build every launchpad transaction (create, publish metadata, attest, launch, commit, execute, claim, fees, swaps), keep a token's metadata on chain (name, symbol, description, a small PNG icon and links, signed by the creator's post-quantum identity; nothing is hosted anywhere), manage post-quantum creator identities (LMS, RFC 8554) and post-quantum vaults (LM-OTS), and write, explain, simulate and run programmable launches (launch rules and autopilot graphs), from Node.js or the browser.

## Status

> **On mainnet, but upgradeable and not finalized. Mainnet protocol not initialized yet. Not audited by an independent firm.**
>
> - **Where it runs.** All five Noised programs (launchpad, Launch Guard transfer hook, autopilot, vault, shield) are deployed on Solana **mainnet** since 2026-10-13 ([docs/MAINNET.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/MAINNET.md)). The mainnet protocol is **not initialized yet** (`initialize_protocol` has not run), so no launch exists on mainnet and `buildCreateLaunchTx` refuses there ("the launchpad protocol account is not initialized"); the vault and the shield do not depend on it. On **devnet**, older builds of the launchpad, hook, autopilot and vault run ([docs/DEVNET.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/DEVNET.md)); the shield is not deployed there. The program ids are the same on every cluster: they are compiled into this SDK (`PROGRAM_IDS`).
> - **Upgradeable.** No program is finalized, so their code can still change. The upgrade authority is `EXgNtEcJ2Co61EQUHfNFN7z8SC3RpmhYKrqcMVcPpJqz` on mainnet (a single key) and the devnet deployer key (`EeGcnw6yAjVC73QdjdtQDqoQgjxDpm2amLWzdoX1Kxvf`) on devnet.
> - **The mainnet autopilot includes review F1.** It judges a price condition across every price observed in its window. SDK 0.9.0 predates that and judges it on the reference price alone, so it can show a price-gated step as due when the program would refuse it; the next release mirrors the program ([CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/sdk/CHANGELOG.md)).
> - **No independent audit.** Neither the programs nor this SDK have been audited by a professional, independent security firm. The reviews so far were internal and AI-assisted (finders, skeptics, proofs of concept and a regression test for every fix), recorded in [docs/AUDIT.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/AUDIT.md). They are not an audit.
> - **SDK 0.9.0.** While the version is `0.x`, a minor release may break the API ([CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/sdk/CHANGELOG.md)).
>
> Do not use Noised with funds you cannot afford to lose. Because no program is final, `checkQsl1` gives no token a QSL-1 level today: at most "candidate".

**Read the [security notes](#security-notes-for-integrators) before you ship anything built on this SDK.** In short: verify before you trust, simulate before you sign, and never sign twice with a one-time post-quantum key.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @noisedlabs/sdk @solana/web3.js
# or
npm install @noisedlabs/sdk @solana/web3.js
```

Pin the exact version you reviewed (`pnpm add -E @noisedlabs/sdk@0.9.0`, or `npm install --save-exact @noisedlabs/sdk@0.9.0`): while the version is `0.x`, a minor release may break the API.

### The peer dependency

`@solana/web3.js` (`^1.98.4`) is the one **peer dependency**: your app provides it, and the SDK uses your copy. That matters because the API takes and returns web3.js objects and checks the `PublicKey` and `Transaction` objects you pass with `instanceof`: objects from a second copy of `@solana/web3.js` would be refused as if they were invalid. The range admits the current 1.x client stack (for example `@solana/wallet-adapter-base` 0.9.28, which needs `^1.99.0`), so npm installs it without `--legacy-peer-deps`; the SDK's own tests run on 1.98.4.

`@solana/spl-token` (0.4.14) and `@coral-xyz/anchor` (0.31.1, only for the `BN` numbers handed to Meteora's quote functions) are ordinary, exactly pinned dependencies: none of their objects crosses the API, and they resolve `@solana/web3.js` to your copy. Meteora's SDK (`@meteora-ag/dynamic-bonding-curve-sdk` 1.5.13), which the SDK loads for swap quotes, lists `@solana/web3.js` as an ordinary dependency with its own range: if your package manager installs a second copy, pin one with `overrides` (pnpm: `overrides` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`; npm: `overrides`; yarn: `resolutions`). The remaining dependencies are `@noble/curves`, `@noble/hashes`, `@scure/bip39` and `buffer`, all exactly pinned.

### Provenance and pinning

Every release is built and published by this repository's release workflow (GitHub Actions) with [npm provenance](https://docs.npmjs.com/generating-provenance-statements). After installing, run:

```bash
npm audit signatures
```

It checks the registry signatures and the provenance attestation of every installed package that has one: for `@noisedlabs/sdk`, that the tarball was built by this repository's workflow from its source. Pin the exact version you reviewed and re-run the check after every upgrade.

### Building from a checkout

Before a release reaches npm, or to use an unreleased commit, build the package from a checkout of this repository and add the tarball to your project:

```bash
cd sdk
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build
pnpm pack                       # writes noised-sdk-<version>.tgz

cd /path/to/your-project
pnpm add /path/to/noised-sdk-<version>.tgz @solana/web3.js
```

## Requirements and compatibility

| | |
|---|---|
| Node.js | 22.12 or later (`engines`). ESM only (`import`, with top-level `await` in your own modules); there is no CommonJS build. |
| Browsers | Through a bundler that supports JSON import attributes (`import x from "./x.json" with { type: "json" }`: the SDK imports its program IDLs this way), such as Vite. The Noised web app bundles the SDK with Vite (target ES2022) and no Node polyfills: the SDK imports the `buffer` package itself. |
| Browser APIs | `crypto.getRandomValues` (keys, seeds, passkey challenges). A leaf or vault-key ledger on Web Storage needs a cross-tab lock: the Web Locks API (`navigator.locks`); the same lock is the recommended `signingLock`. Passkey identities need an authenticator with the WebAuthn **PRF** extension and user verification (feature-detect it and fall back to the 24-word phrase). `CompressionStream("deflate")` is used when present to compress icons (`encodeIndexedPng` falls back to stored blocks without it). |
| TypeScript | Types are included (`dist/*.d.ts`, built with TypeScript 6, `strict`). Use `moduleResolution` `node16`, `nodenext` or `bundler`, which read the package's `exports` (needed for `@noisedlabs/sdk/programmable` and `@noisedlabs/sdk/idl/<name>.json`). The old `node` (node10) resolution cannot see them. |
| Solana | `@solana/web3.js` `^1.98.4`, provided by your app (`Connection`, `PublicKey`, `Keypair`, `Transaction`; tested on 1.98.4). Transactions over the legacy size limit are built in the v1 format (SIMD-0385) as raw signed bytes. |

The package has three entry points:

| Import | What |
|---|---|
| `@noisedlabs/sdk` | Everything: builders, account readers, verifiers, QSL-1, post-quantum identities and vaults, and everything of `/programmable`. Four modules are namespaces: `pqIdentity`, `leafLedger`, `lms` and `lmots`. |
| `@noisedlabs/sdk/programmable` | The pure programmable-launch module (launch rules, autopilot graphs, their text languages, explainers and simulators), without the Solana client stack. |
| `@noisedlabs/sdk/idl/<name>.json` | The program IDLs the SDK encodes with: `noised_launchpad`, `noised_hook`, `noised_vault`, `noised_shield`, `noised_autopilot`, `dynamic_bonding_curve`, `cp_amm`. |

## Quickstart

Five minutes, read-only, against devnet. Nothing here signs or sends anything. The mint is one of the devnet test tokens of [docs/DEVNET.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/DEVNET.md) ("Phalanx Devnet B", a custom launch with one launch rule; it carries the project's earlier name because it was launched before the rename).

```ts
import { Connection, PublicKey } from "@solana/web3.js";
import { assertCluster, checkQsl1, fetchLaunchByMint, getLaunchFlowStatus, qslBadge, verifyLaunch } from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

// 1. Connect, and check that this RPC really serves devnet (by its genesis hash, never by its URL).
const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");
await assertCluster(conn, "devnet"); // throws ClusterMismatchError otherwise

// 2. A devnet test token.
const mint = new PublicKey("4QQ2L5ptTtrGyMqPbQ7DSiEmD58GPHKvpRcJDdbVos73");

// 3. Read its launch and where it stands.
const launch = await fetchLaunchByMint(conn, mint);
if (launch === null) throw new Error("not a Noised launch");
const status = await getLaunchFlowStatus(conn, launch.publicKey);
console.log(launch.market?.name, launch.market?.symbol, "|", status.step, "|", status.summary);

// 4. Check it against QSL-1 and turn the result into a badge.
const result = await checkQsl1(conn, mint); // reads at "finalized"; levels exist on mainnet only
const badge = qslBadge(result);
console.log(badge.title, "for", badge.mint); // on devnet: "QSL-1 candidate: not final yet"
for (const line of badge.lines) console.log("  " + line);
if (badge.programmable !== null) console.log(badge.programmable.text, "-", badge.programmable.link);

// 5. Re-check everything from live accounts: the certificate is never trusted on its own.
const report = await verifyLaunch(conn, mint);
console.log("verifyLaunch:", report.overall);
for (const c of report.checks) if (c.status !== "pass") console.log(`  ${c.status} ${c.id}: ${c.label} (${c.detail})`);
```

What you should see (checked against devnet while writing this): the badge says "QSL-1 candidate: not final yet", with the lines "Meets every check for Level 2 (Quantum-attested), but no level is given yet", why (the programs can still be updated; this is devnet), and the launch rule's warning "For the first 30 minutes, some wallet-to-wallet transfers are limited (rule 1)". The programmable tag reads just "programmable - read its rules": the "QSL-1 L2 · programmable" form appears only next to an awarded level. `verifyLaunch` reports `warn` with no failing check: its warnings name the Noised programs that can still be upgraded and the Meteora and Token-2022 programs whose code or authority changed since the slots the SDK reviewed (`TRUST_ANCHORS`). The public devnet RPC rate-limits hard: if you see `429 Too Many Requests`, retry or use your own devnet RPC.

From here: [read launches](#reading-launches), [verify tokens](#verifying-a-token-and-showing-a-qsl-1-badge), or [launch one](#quick-launch-end-to-end).

## Concepts

### How the SDK works

- **Builders never send.** A `build…Tx` function reads the chain, refuses what the program would refuse, and returns either a legacy `Transaction` (fee payer and recent blockhash set; signed only where the docs say so, for example by a fresh mint keypair) or **signed v1 wire bytes** (`Uint8Array`) for transactions that exceed the legacy format or are paid by a throwaway key. Nothing reaches the network unless you call a `send…` function or send the transaction yourself. Several steps have a `buildPlanned…` form that takes a plan object instead of loose arguments.
- **Program parity.** Every instruction and account is encoded and decoded from the program IDLs shipped in `dist/idl/` (also importable as `@noisedlabs/sdk/idl/<name>.json`), so account order and signer and writable flags come from the programs themselves. Every encoder, hasher and signer is tested byte for byte against vectors produced by the Rust programs and crates.
- **Numbers and time.** `bigint` for every u64, u128 and i64: lamports, token base units, slots, unix timestamps. `number` for u8, u16 and u32 (basis points, leaf indexes, key indexes). Times are **unix seconds**, never `Date.now()` milliseconds. Every "now" is a `bigint` named `nowSecs` (`launchPhase`, `batchOutcome`, `verifyLaunch`, the launch builders, the launch flow and the window helpers), because the chain's clock and every timestamp the SDK decodes are i64: a `number` is refused with a `TypeError`, a value that looks like milliseconds (10^11 or more) with a `RangeError`, so `inLaunchWindow(BigInt(Date.now()), …)` throws instead of saying "not in the window". Use `unixNowSecs()` (local clock) or `clusterUnixTime(conn)` (the cluster's, what the programs compare with). Every time the post-quantum identity signs is also returned as an absolute UTC date (`windowIso`, `activateAtIso`, `notAfterIso`; `unixToIso`, `unixToUtcText`): show those, not only "in an hour".
- **Errors.** Builders throw an `Error` with a plain-English reason. When it pre-empts a program error, the reason names it (for example `InvalidPayoutOwner: …` or `NotLaunchWindow: …`). The refusals you must handle in a UI are typed classes: see [Errors](#errors).
- **Post-quantum signing is guarded.** The signing entry points (`buildAttestLaunchTx` / `buildPlannedAttestTx`, `buildPqAuthorizeTx`, `prepareWithdrawal`, `signWithdrawal`) first check that the RPC serves the cluster the keys belong to (genesis hash), take a durable ledger (no default) in which the one-time key is reserved for its message before any signature exists and the signature is recorded before it is returned, sign deterministically (a retry gives identical bytes), and refuse anything that would make a one-time key sign a second message. Before the identity signs a time, the RPC's clock must agree with this device's (and a second RPC's when given). The vault signers also require the user's confirmation of the recipient check (`RecipientConfirmation`). What a signer signs is what it was given at the call: the request, message, key and confirmation are copied at entry, so an object edited while the call awaits the network (a reactive form) changes nothing. No public path exposes a raw one-time signer: `lmots` has no `sign`, `LmsKeyPair` no signing method (the raw signers are internal modules, outside the package's `exports`).
- **Throwaway fee payers.** The post-quantum steps (`publish_metadata`, `publish_rules`, `attest_launch`, `pq_authorize`, vault withdrawals) are paid by a fresh Ed25519 key with no authority over anything, funded by the wallet just before and swept back after (`throwawayPayerFunding`, `buildFundThrowawayPayerTx`, `buildSweepPayerTx`; for vaults `buildFundFeePayerTx`, `buildRefundFeePayerTx`). Keep its secret key durably until it is swept: an interrupted run finds its lamports there.
- **Fees and compute.** The launch builders, the publish and attest builders, the autopilot builders and the vault's withdraw and release builders take `{ computeUnitPrice?: bigint, computeUnitLimit?: number }` (`ComputeBudgetOptions`) as their last argument. By default they set a tight, measured compute-unit limit and no priority fee. `buildSwapTx` takes them too, opt-in (without them the swap is left as Meteora built it). A `computeUnitPrice` (micro-lamports per compute unit) adds one; in v1 transactions it becomes the priority-fee word, `ceil(price × limit / 1,000,000)` lamports.

### QSL-1, the token standard

QSL-1 ("Quantum Security Layer token, v1", [docs/standard/QSL-1.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/standard/QSL-1.md), revision 0.4) defines a class of Solana tokens and how anyone recognizes them from live accounts. It has two nested levels:

| Level | Name | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | No-rug | Nobody, the creator included, can mint more, freeze holders, change the metadata, withdraw the graduated liquidity, block sales or redirect fees. |
| L2 | Quantum-attested | L1, and the launch went live only because the creator's post-quantum identity (a hash-based LMS key) signed its parameters, its on-chain metadata record and its launch window. The signature is re-verified from account state. |

**"Programmable" is not a level.** A token whose creator added launch rules (extra limits on transfers during the first hours, bound on-chain and signed with the launch) or automation (an autopilot plan for its treasury) is described as programmable next to its level: "QSL-1 L2 · programmable", with a link to read its rules. That is a description, never a safety claim: rules can limit who can buy or move tokens for a while, and automation can be run or changed by people the creator chose.

`checkQsl1(conn, mint)` runs the standard's verification algorithm (its §7) condition by condition (C1.1 to C1.24, C2.1 to C2.8) and returns the level, every check with a plain-English sentence, the reasons the next level is not reached, who you still trust, and `programmable`: the rules and automation, their checks (P.R1 to P.R4, P.G1 to P.G5) and the warnings. Two rules decide whether a level is given at all:

- **Mainnet only.** Noised's program ids are the same on every cluster, so a level exists only for mainnet-beta (checked by genesis hash).
- **Final programs only.** While the Noised launchpad (and, while the hook is active, the Launch Guard) can still be upgraded, no level is given (condition C1.24): a mint that meets everything else is a **candidate** (`candidate: true`, `wouldBe` its level). Today every Noised token is at most a candidate.

`qslBadge(result)` turns the result into what an app may show, in the standard's own words (its Appendix A): "QSL-1 · No-rug", "QSL-1 · Quantum-attested", "QSL-1 candidate: not final yet" or "Not QSL-1", with the lines it may add and the lines it must show next to the badge, and, when rules or automation are present, the "programmable" tag.

### The life of a launch

```text
 creator wallet       throwaway payer                  post-quantum identity     anyone
 ──────────────       ───────────────                  ─────────────────────     ──────
 create_launch  ──►   publish_metadata
 (wait: finalized)    [publish_rules]        ──►       attest_launch (signs)
 fund the payer       (wait: finalized)                [pq_authorize: autopilot]
                      sweep back to the wallet
                                                                                 launch (inside the signed window)
                                                                                 commit ─► execute_batch ─► claim
                                                                                 trading under the Launch Guard
                                                                                 graduation ─► migration to DAMM v2
                                                                                 claim_fees / claim_lp_fees ─► distribute
                                                                                 autopilot runs (keepers)
```

The creator's wallet creates the launch (a classical Ed25519 signature). The token's metadata record, and the launch rules if any, are published from a throwaway payer and must be final. Then the creator's post-quantum identity signs the exact parameters, the record's hash, the rules' hash and a time window: without that signature the token can never go live. Inside the window anyone may send `launch`. The first minutes are a fair-open batch (everyone gets the same price, pro rata above the cap), then the Launch Guard limits buys and wallet sizes for the launch's guard period (6 hours in the Fair preset; at least the batch window plus 10 minutes, at most 72 hours), then the token trades freely on its bonding curve until it graduates to a Meteora DAMM v2 pool whose liquidity nobody can withdraw.

## Guide

Every snippet below is an ES module with top-level `await` and shows its imports. Values you must supply (your wallet, your phrase, a durable store) are written as `declare const`; replace them with your own. In an app, the wallet signs through its adapter where the snippets call `tx.partialSign(wallet)`.

### Connection and cluster checks

Every function takes a `@solana/web3.js` `Connection`. Builders fetch their blockhash at `"confirmed"`, and readers read at `"confirmed"`, except `checkQsl1` (`"finalized"` by default); `waitForTokenMeta` and `waitForLaunchRules` wait until a record is `"finalized"`.

Noised's program ids, vault addresses and launch addresses are **the same on every cluster**, and nothing inside a post-quantum signature says which cluster it is for. A "devnet" run whose endpoint is really mainnet would therefore make signatures that are valid on mainnet. So every post-quantum signing function calls `assertCluster` with the cluster its keys were derived for and refuses on any mismatch (`ClusterMismatchError`); localnet is refused unless you pass `allowLocalnet: true`. Call it yourself too, before showing anything cluster-specific.

```ts
import { Connection } from "@solana/web3.js";
import {
  assertCluster, checkClockSkew, ClockSkewError, ClusterMismatchError, clusterOfGenesisHash, clusterUnixTime, GENESIS_HASHES,
  unixNowSecs, unixToIso,
} from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const secondRpcUrl: string; // a second, independent devnet RPC (another provider)

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");
const second = new Connection(secondRpcUrl, "confirmed");

try {
  const genesis = await assertCluster(conn, "devnet"); // returns the genesis hash
  console.log(genesis === GENESIS_HASHES.devnet); // true
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof ClusterMismatchError) console.error(`expected ${e.expected}, the RPC serves ${e.actual ?? "another cluster"} (${e.genesisHash})`);
  throw e;
}

// Which cluster is an endpoint, whatever its URL says? "mainnet", "devnet", or null (local or private).
console.log(clusterOfGenesisHash(await second.getGenesisHash()));

// Time is bigint unix seconds everywhere: this device's clock, and the cluster's (what the programs compare with).
console.log(unixToIso(unixNowSecs()), unixToIso(await clusterUnixTime(conn)));

// Before the identity signs a time, the SDK checks the clocks; you can run the same check up front.
try {
  const clock = await checkClockSkew(conn, { secondConnection: second }); // at most CLOCK_SKEW_MAX_SECS (120 s) apart
  console.log(`clocks agree within ${clock.skewSecs} s; cluster time ${unixToIso(clock.clusterSecs)}`);
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof ClockSkewError) console.error(e.message); // nothing that names a time will be signed until this is fixed
  else throw e;
}
```

`clusterUnixTime` refuses a clock that is not plausible unix seconds and names the RPC. The signing builders take the same clock options (`localNowSecs`, `secondConnection`, `maxClockSkewSecs`); pass `secondConnection` whenever you have a second provider, so that one dishonest RPC cannot shift what the identity signs.

### Reading launches

```ts
import { Connection, PublicKey } from "@solana/web3.js";
import {
  batchOutcome, CERTIFICATE_RULES_BOUND, certificateChecksComplete, clusterUnixTime, expectedBatchFill, fetchCertificate,
  fetchHookPolicy, fetchLaunch, fetchLaunchByMint, getLaunchFlowStatus, launchPhase, listLaunches,
} from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");
const mint = new PublicKey("4QQ2L5ptTtrGyMqPbQ7DSiEmD58GPHKvpRcJDdbVos73");

// By mint (through its certificate) or by launch address. Null when there is none.
const launch = await fetchLaunchByMint(conn, mint);
if (launch === null) throw new Error("no Noised launch for this mint");
const same = await fetchLaunch(conn, launch.publicKey);
console.log(same?.creator.toBase58(), launch.guardSecs, launch.migrationQuoteThreshold);

// Phases come from the cluster clock: configured | commit | execute | guarded | open | graduated.
const now = await clusterUnixTime(conn);
console.log(launchPhase(launch, now), batchOutcome(launch, now)); // batch: pending | executed | expired | empty

// The market snapshot (live launches): name, symbol, supply, the curve's reserves and price, graduation.
const m = launch.market;
if (m !== undefined) console.log(m.name, m.symbol, `${m.quoteReserve} lamports in the curve`, m.curveComplete, m.migrated, m.dammPool?.toBase58());

// Where the launch flow stands, in one plain sentence (and the attested window as UTC dates).
const status = await getLaunchFlowStatus(conn, launch.publicKey, { nowSecs: now });
console.log(status.step, status.summary, status.windowIso);

// The fair-open batch. While it takes commits: what a 1 SOL commit would get if it executed now (above the cap,
// commits fill pro rata). Once executed: the exact fill (an extra commit then throws a RangeError).
if (!launch.executed) {
  const fill = expectedBatchFill(launch, 1_000_000_000n);
  console.log(`a 1 SOL commit now: spent ${fill.commit.spent}, refunded ${fill.commit.refund} lamports, oversubscribed: ${fill.oversubscribed}`);
} else {
  const fill = expectedBatchFill(launch);
  console.log(`the batch spent ${fill.fill} of ${fill.totalCommitted} lamports (${fill.fillBps / 100}% of each commit)`);
}

// The launch certificate: test the twelve required bits with a MASK. A launch with creator rules also sets
// RULES_BOUND (4096), so its checks are 8,191: comparing with === 4095 would call it incomplete.
const cert = await fetchCertificate(conn, mint);
if (cert !== null) {
  console.log(`version ${cert.version}, all required checks: ${certificateChecksComplete(cert.checks)}, rules bound: ${(cert.checks & CERTIFICATE_RULES_BOUND) !== 0}`);
}

// The Launch Guard's live policy: the guard's end, the caps, and the creator rules it enforces.
const policy = await fetchHookPolicy(conn, mint);
console.log(policy?.guardEndTs, policy?.rules.length);

// Every launch of the launchpad: one getProgramAccounts, which many public RPCs refuse or rate-limit.
const all = await listLaunches(conn);
console.log(`${all.length} launches`);
```

Always test certificate checks with `(checks & 4095) === 4095` (`certificateChecksComplete(checks)`, or `certificateComplete(cert)`), **never** `checks === 4095`. A certificate is only what the launchpad recorded at launch: to know whether a token is safe now, use `verifyLaunch` or `checkQsl1` (next section).

`getLaunchFlowStatus` tells a UI what comes next for a launch: `create`, `publish` (pass `expectedMetadataHash` / `expectedRulesHash` from your plan), `attest`, `wait-for-window`, `launch`, `window-missed` ("Window passed: sign a new opening time"), `commit`, `execute`, `claim` or `trading`, with `secondsUntilWindowOpens`, `canLaunchNow` and `warnings`. With `pending: { ledger, lmsPublicKey }` it also lists the identity's signatures for this launch that never landed (see [when the identity refuses to sign](#when-the-identity-refuses-to-sign)).

### Verifying a token and showing a QSL-1 badge

Two checkers, both from live accounts only: `verifyLaunch` (every Noised launch check, with the launch's post-quantum origin, its metadata record and its launch rules) and `checkQsl1` (the QSL-1 standard's algorithm, condition by condition).

```ts
import { Connection, PublicKey } from "@solana/web3.js";
import { checkQsl1, qslBadge, verifyLaunch } from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");
const mint = new PublicKey("4QQ2L5ptTtrGyMqPbQ7DSiEmD58GPHKvpRcJDdbVos73");

// --- verifyLaunch: fail, warn or pass, check by check ---
const report = await verifyLaunch(conn, mint);
if (report.overall === "fail") console.log("not a safe Noised launch");
for (const c of report.checks) console.log(c.status, c.label, c.detail);
for (const p of report.trustedParties) console.log("still trusted:", p.name, p.note);

// The post-quantum origin, re-verified: show it only when verified is true.
if (report.pqOrigin?.verified === true) console.log(`signed by its creator's post-quantum identity (leaf ${report.pqOrigin.leaf})`);

// The token's own metadata record, read from chain and re-checked (nothing is fetched from a link).
const md = report.metadata;
if (md?.verified === true && md.document?.ok === true) {
  console.log(md.document.description, md.document.icon?.dataUri); // an <img src> under CSP img-src data:
  for (const l of md.document.links) console.log(`${l.url} (goes to ${l.host})`); // inert text, never opened automatically
}

// The creator's launch rules, in plain English, as bound on chain.
if (report.rules?.verified === true) for (const line of report.rules.explanation) console.log(line);

// --- checkQsl1 + qslBadge: what an app may show ---
const result = await checkQsl1(conn, mint);
const badge = qslBadge(result);
console.log(badge.title, badge.mint, badge.tone); // "QSL-1 candidate: not final yet" on devnet
for (const line of badge.lines) console.log(line); // what the badge may say, then what must be shown next to it
if (!badge.showOnTradeScreen) console.log("(a candidate: show it only on a known test cluster, or in developer views)");
for (const c of result.checks) console.log(c.id, c.status, c.plain); // "C1.5 pass Nobody can mint more of this token."
console.log(result.reasons); // why the next level is not reached, in plain English
if (badge.programmable !== null) {
  // "QSL-1 L2 · programmable - read its rules" next to a level; "programmable - read its rules" for a candidate.
  console.log(badge.programmable.text, "-", badge.programmable.link);
  for (const w of badge.programmable.warnings) console.log("!", w); // "For the first 30 minutes, some wallet-to-wallet ..."
  for (const line of badge.programmable.explain) console.log(line); // what "read its rules" opens
}
```

How to display it:

- Show a badge only from `qslBadge(await checkQsl1(conn, mint))`, never from the certificate's flags. Keep the mint address next to it (`badge.mint`), let the badge open the full list of `result.checks` and `result.trusted` (who can still change the outcome), and show `badge.required` lines whenever the badge is shown.
- A candidate goes on a trade screen only where `badge.showOnTradeScreen` is true (a cluster known not to be mainnet); on mainnet, and when the cluster is `unknown`, show it only in developer views.
- Show "programmable" as `badge.programmable.text` next to the level with its "read its rules" link and its warnings: never as a level, never as "safer".
- Never call a token "quantum-proof", "audited" or "verified" (QSL-1 Appendix A.3).
- For decisions of consequence, run the checks against a second, independent RPC provider and compare: a report is only as honest as the RPC that served it.

Before launch, `verifyAttestation(conn, launch)` re-verifies an attestation, its identity, its record, its rules and its LMS signature from live accounts (for an "upcoming launches" list: show the record and "signed by its creator's post-quantum identity" only when `verified`). Indexers that already hold the accounts can run `evaluateQsl1(snapshot)`, the same evaluation without RPC reads. A complete script: [`sdk/examples/verify-mint.ts`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/sdk/examples/verify-mint.ts).

### Quick launch, end to end

`planQuickLaunch` turns a short form into everything a launch needs: the Fair preset with your trading fee, the fee recipients, the metadata record, and, when fees go to the treasury, the autopilot's daily buyback-and-burn graph. It is pure (nothing is read or sent) and throws one `Error` listing every problem. Its result:

- `plan`: the full `LaunchPlan` (when you pass `opensAt`); `launch`, `launchSeed`, `params`, `recipients`, `treasury`, `metadata`, `metadataHash`, `launchInput` (to call `planLaunch` yourself with a later opening time).
- `graph`: `{ template: "daily-buyback-burn", bytes, hash, explanation, publishVia }` (null when every fee goes to the wallet).
- `steps`: the ordered list of what the app runs, each `{ id, title, detail, signer, sdk, when }` in plain English, `signer` being `"creator-wallet"`, `"throwaway-payer"`, `"pq-identity"` or `"anyone"`. For `feeDestination: "buyback-burn"` they are: `create-launch`, `fund-helper`, `save-token-details`, `approve-launch`, `set-up-autopilot`, `save-autopilot-plan`, `approve-autopilot-plan`, `switch-on-autopilot`, `start-autopilot-plan`, `return-helper-sol`, `go-live`, `connect-autopilot-token`, `pay-out-fees`, `connect-autopilot-pool`, `daily-buyback`. With `"wallet"` the autopilot steps are left out.
- `summary` (plain-English lines for the creator) and `warnings`.

The form: `name` (1..=32 bytes), `symbol` (1..=10 bytes), optional `description` (at most 500 bytes), `website` (an `https://` link) and `x` (an `https://x.com/…` link), `iconPng` (a PNG of at most 64x64, `encodeIndexedPng`), `feeBps` (`QUICK_LAUNCH_FEE_BPS_RANGE`: 25 to 833, so the fee plus its busy-market extra stays within the 10% ceiling), `feeDestination` (`"wallet"`, `"buyback-burn"`, or `{ split: walletBps }`), `creator`, `identity`, and optionally `opensAt`, `windowSecs`, `nowSecs`, `launchSeed` and `buyback` (`{ solPerBuyback, premiumBps, minTreasurySol }` within `QUICK_LAUNCH_BUYBACK_RANGES`; defaults `QUICK_LAUNCH_BUYBACK_DEFAULTS`: 0.5 SOL a day, at most 3% above the recent low, only with 0.5 SOL in the treasury; a premium below what covers the pool's 1% fee, 102 bps, is refused because such a buyback could never fill).

The script below runs the steps in that order. It mirrors what the devnet test run does ([`scripts/devnet/20-flow-a.mjs`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/scripts/devnet/20-flow-a.mjs) with [`launch-steps.mjs`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/scripts/devnet/launch-steps.mjs)), and the order the web app follows ([`app/src/lib/launchFlow.ts`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/app/src/lib/launchFlow.ts)). On devnet, that script ran this flow up to the graduation buy; graduation, migration, fees and the buyback ran on a local fork of devnet ([docs/DEVNET.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/DEVNET.md)). In production, persist what rebuilds the plan exactly (the form's inputs with the icon's PNG bytes, the `launchSeed` and the `opensAt`), the throwaway payer's key and the graph activation plan (its `activateAt` is signed), so a reload resumes where it stopped: every step reads the chain first, and a rebuilt signature is the same leaf and the same bytes. The devnet script does exactly this (`loadOrMakePlan` in `launch-steps.mjs`).

```ts
import { Connection, Keypair, type Transaction } from "@solana/web3.js";
import {
  assertCluster, buildBindMintTx, buildFundThrowawayPayerTx, buildNextGraphActivationTx, buildPlannedAttestTx,
  buildPlannedCreateLaunchTx, buildPlannedLaunchTx, buildPlannedPublishTx, buildSweepPayerTx, clusterUnixTime,
  encodeIndexedPng, fundingLamportsForAuthorize, getGraphActivationStatus, leafLedger, planGraphActivation, planQuickLaunch,
  pqIdentity, sendAndConfirm, sendAttestLaunchTx, sendPqAuthorizeTx, sendPublishMetadataTx, simulateAndExplain,
  throwawayPayerFunding, waitForLaunchWindow, waitForTokenMeta,
  type lms,
} from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const creator: Keypair;                        // the creator's wallet (in an app, its adapter signs)
declare const phrase: string;                          // the 24-word post-quantum phrase, kept apart from any wallet
declare const iconRgba: Uint8Array;                    // a 32x32 icon, RGBA (4 bytes per pixel), e.g. from a canvas
declare const ledgerStore: leafLedger.LeafLedgerStore; // durable, with an atomic add: see "The leaf ledger"
declare const treeCache: lms.LmsTreeCacheStore;        // optional: the identity then loads in milliseconds

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");
await assertCluster(conn, "devnet");

/** Simulate, refuse surprises, add the wallet's signature (keeping any already there), send. */
async function send(tx: Transaction, finalized = false): Promise<string> {
  const sim = await simulateAndExplain(conn, tx);
  if (!sim.ok) throw new Error(`simulation failed: ${sim.error ?? "unknown error"}`);
  if (sim.unknownPrograms.length > 0) throw new Error("refusing to sign: the transaction calls programs this SDK does not know");
  tx.partialSign(creator);
  return sendAndConfirm(conn, tx, finalized ? { commitment: "finalized" } : {});
}

// 0. The creator's post-quantum identity, and its durable leaf ledger.
const secret = pqIdentity.importMaster(phrase);
const identity = await pqIdentity.deriveIdentity(secret.master, "devnet", 0, { cache: treeCache });
const ledger = leafLedger.createLeafLedger(ledgerStore);

// 1. The plan: it fixes everything the identity will sign (parameters, record, window).
const now = await clusterUnixTime(conn); // the CLUSTER clock, in seconds
const quick = planQuickLaunch({
  name: "Example",
  symbol: "EXMPL",
  description: "A fair-launched example token.",
  website: "https://example.org",
  iconPng: await encodeIndexedPng(iconRgba, 32, 32, 16),
  feeBps: 100,                    // a 1% trading fee
  feeDestination: "buyback-burn", // the creator's share goes to the launch's autopilot treasury
  creator: creator.publicKey,
  identity,
  opensAt: now + 900n,            // the launch window opens in 15 minutes, for an hour
  nowSecs: now,
});
const { plan, graph } = quick;
if (plan === null || graph === null) throw new Error("unreachable: opensAt was given and fees go to the treasury");
for (const line of quick.summary) console.log(line);
for (const w of quick.warnings) console.warn(w);
for (const s of quick.steps) console.log(`${s.id} [${s.signer}] ${s.title}: ${s.sdk}`);

// 2. create_launch: the wallet signs. The identity signs only a FINALIZED launch (about 13 s after confirmation).
const created = await buildPlannedCreateLaunchTx(conn, plan);
for (const w of created.warnings) console.warn(w);
await send(created.tx, true);

// 3. Fund a throwaway fee payer: the metadata record, the attestation and the autopilot approval.
const payer = Keypair.generate(); // persist its secret key until it is swept
const funding = await throwawayPayerFunding(conn, { metadata: plan.metadata, launch: plan.launch, lmsPublicKey: identity.publicKey });
const forApproval = await fundingLamportsForAuthorize(conn); // pq_authorize lands from the same payer
const fund = await buildFundThrowawayPayerTx(conn, creator.publicKey, payer.publicKey, { lamports: funding.lamports + forApproval });
await send(fund.tx);

// 4. The token's metadata record (name, symbol, description, icon, links), FINALIZED before the identity signs:
//    a record lost in a dropped fork would turn the attestation into a burned leaf.
const published = await buildPlannedPublishTx(conn, plan, payer); // "ready", or "already-published"
if (published.status === "ready") await sendPublishMetadataTx(conn, published);
await waitForTokenMeta(conn, plan.launch, plan.metadataHash); // default: finalized

// 5. attest_launch: the identity signs (its leaf reserved in the ledger first), the throwaway payer lands it.
const attest = await buildPlannedAttestTx(conn, plan, { identity, ledger, payer });
if (attest.status === "ready") {
  const outcome = await sendAttestLaunchTx(conn, attest, { ledger }); // "attested", "burned" or "pending"
  if (outcome.status !== "attested") throw new Error(`not attested (${outcome.status}): ${outcome.detail}`);
} else if (attest.status === "leaf-landed") {
  throw new Error(`leaf ${attest.leaf} already landed: confirmAttestation tells what it did; never sign again blindly`);
} // "already-attested": nothing to do

// 6. The autopilot: init_autopilot, publish_graph, pq_authorize (kind 1, the identity), activate, apply_pending.
//    A first graph may start at once; the start time is part of what the identity signs, so keep this plan.
const activation = await planGraphActivation(conn, plan.launch, graph.bytes, { marginSecs: 45n });
console.log(`the autopilot plan starts at ${activation.activateAtIso}`, activation.warnings);
for (;;) {
  const next = await buildNextGraphActivationTx(conn, plan.launch, activation, {
    payer: creator.publicKey, // pays the legacy steps
    throwaway: payer,         // pays the approval (and a graph too large for a legacy publish)
    identity,
    ledger,
    creator: creator.publicKey,
  });
  if (next === null) {
    const s = await getGraphActivationStatus(conn, plan.launch, activation);
    if (s.next !== "wait" || s.applyAt === null) {
      console.log(s.stage, s.plain); // "active" once running
      break;
    }
    const secs = s.applyAt - (await clusterUnixTime(conn)); // queued: wait for activate_at on the cluster clock
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, Math.max(1, Number(secs) + 1) * 1_000));
    continue;
  }
  console.log(next.status.plain);
  switch (next.step) {
    case "init-autopilot":
    case "activate":
    case "apply-pending":
      await send(next.result);
      break;
    case "publish-graph": {
      const r = next.result;
      if (r.status === "already-published") break;
      if ("lastValidBlockHeight" in r) await sendAndConfirm(conn, r.tx, { lastValidBlockHeight: r.lastValidBlockHeight }); // v1, signed by the payer
      else await send(r.tx); // fits a legacy transaction (the 122-byte daily graph does)
      break;
    }
    case "authorize": {
      const r = next.result;
      if (r.status === "ready") {
        const outcome = await sendPqAuthorizeTx(conn, r, { ledger });
        if (outcome.status !== "authorized") throw new Error(`approval not written (${outcome.status}): ${outcome.detail}`);
      } else if (r.status === "leaf-landed") {
        throw new Error(`leaf ${r.leaf} landed without this approval: confirmAuthorization tells what it did`);
      }
      break;
    }
  }
}

// 7. Return what is left on the throwaway payer, and wipe the secrets.
const sweep = await buildSweepPayerTx(conn, payer, creator.publicKey); // already signed by the payer
if (sweep !== null) await sendAndConfirm(conn, sweep.tx);
identity.keyPair.wipe();
pqIdentity.wipeMaster(secret);

// 8. Go live inside the attested window. Anyone may send launch; the first one to land wins.
await waitForLaunchWindow(conn, plan.launch);
const mint = Keypair.generate();
const { tx: launchTx } = await buildPlannedLaunchTx(conn, plan, creator.publicKey, mint); // signed by the mint keypair
await send(launchTx); // partialSign keeps the mint's signature

// 9. Connect the autopilot to the new mint (anyone may send it).
await send(await buildBindMintTx(conn, creator.publicKey, plan.launch));
console.log(`live: ${mint.publicKey.toBase58()}`);
```

What comes next, in the order of `quick.steps`:

- **The fair-open batch** (`commit`, `execute_batch`, `claim`): see [commit, claim, swaps and fees](#commit-claim-swaps-and-fees).
- **Fees** (`pay-out-fees`): anyone sends `buildClaimFeesTx` (bonding-curve fees), after graduation `buildClaimLpFeesTx`, then `buildDistributeTx`, which pays the platform share and then the creator's share to the recipients, here the autopilot treasury.
- **Graduation** (`connect-autopilot-pool`): once the curve completes and Meteora migrates the liquidity to DAMM v2, anyone sends `buildBindPoolTx`; buybacks can run from then on.
- **The daily buyback** (`daily-buyback`): a keeper runs it, see [the keeper loop](#keepers).

Notes:

- If nobody launches inside the window, the step becomes `window-missed`: plan a new window for the same launch and record (`replanLaunchWindow(plan, { opensAt, nowSecs })`), then `buildPlannedAttestTx` again. The identity signs it at its next leaf, which replaces the unused attestation. An earlier signature that was sent but never landed can take that place first, so the SDK refuses a new window while one is pending (`PendingAttestationError`): see [when the identity refuses to sign](#when-the-identity-refuses-to-sign).
- Want the fees in post-quantum custody instead? Use `planLaunch` with `feeVault` (the wSOL vault from `prepareFeeVault`) or with recipients that are PQ vaults: [`sdk/examples/launch-with-pq-identity.ts`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/sdk/examples/launch-with-pq-identity.ts) does exactly that, and persists its plan, ledger and payer on disk so it resumes after an interruption.
- Wallets and explorers show the token's name and symbol from the mint; the icon, description and links show in Noised and in anything that reads the record (`fetchTokenMetaForMint`). The mint's uri stays empty unless the creator signs a uri mode: `METADATA.FLAG_EXTERNAL_URI` (the creator's own `https://` link, whose content can change) or `METADATA.FLAG_INLINE_URI` (the document inline as a `data:` uri; do not offer it until wallets and indexers are shown to list such tokens).

### Custom launch with launch rules

Launch rules (PXR1 bytes) add restrictions to the Launch Guard while it is on: deny buys or wallet-to-wallet transfers, or cap an amount or the receiving account's balance, under conditions (a buy, time since launch, amount, wallets, the program a transfer goes through, the transaction's instruction count). **Rules can only refuse.** Sells are always allowed, the batch and its claims are decided before any rule runs, rules never apply to holders moving tokens through the Noised vault or shield directly, and every rule ends with the guard (72 hours at most).

The devnet test run [`scripts/devnet/30-flow-b.mjs`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/scripts/devnet/30-flow-b.mjs) launched a token with this one rule and a 30-minute guard: a 2,000-token wallet-to-wallet transfer was refused on chain (`RuleDenied`, hook error 6011), a 500-token one passed, and the same wallet's sell passed ([docs/DEVNET.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/DEVNET.md)).

**Write and check the rules** (pure: `@noisedlabs/sdk/programmable`, also re-exported from the root):

```ts
import {
  compileRules, explainRules, parseRules, printRules, rules, ruleWarnings, rulesHashHex, simulateTransfer, tryParseRules,
  verifyRules, when,
} from "@noisedlabs/sdk/programmable";

const GUARD_SECS = 1_800; // the launch's guardSecs: rules are verified against it

// As text (the rules language: sdk/src/programmable/README.md)...
const text = `rules v1
guard 30m
always: deny when p2p and amount > 1000 tokens code P2P
`;
const parsed = tryParseRules(text, { guardSecs: GUARD_SECS }); // every error, with line, column and a hint
if (!parsed.ok) for (const e of parsed.errors) console.error(e.pretty);
const set = parseRules(text, { guardSecs: GUARD_SECS }); // or throw a DslError at the first one

// ...or as code. Both compile to the same 62 bytes.
const bytes = compileRules(set, { guardSecs: GUARD_SECS });
const sameBytes = rules({ guardSecs: GUARD_SECS }).deny(when.p2p().and(when.amountGt(1000)), "P2P").compile();

// The chain's own verifier, and the hash the attestation will sign.
const verdict = verifyRules(bytes, { guardSecs: GUARD_SECS });
if (!verdict.ok) throw new Error(`${verdict.code}: ${verdict.message}`);
console.log(verdict.hashHex === rulesHashHex(sameBytes)); // true: b92b1a1e…

// What holders should read: the rules in plain English, and the warnings QSL-1 shows next to "programmable".
for (const line of explainRules(bytes)) console.log(line);
for (const w of ruleWarnings(bytes, { guardSecs: GUARD_SECS })) console.log(w.kind, w.plain); // transferLimits: ...

// Try transfers the way the hook decides them.
for (const [kind, amount] of [["p2p", 2_000], ["p2p", 500], ["sell", 2_000]] as const) {
  const v = simulateTransfer(set, { kind, at: "10m", amount });
  console.log(kind, amount, v.allowed ? "allowed" : `refused (${v.refusal}, ${v.codeName})`, "-", v.why);
}
console.log(printRules(set)); // the canonical text
```

Templates fit real launches (`RULE_TEMPLATES`, `ruleTemplate(id, params)`, combined with `mergeRuleSets`): `fair-start`, `anti-bot` (a limit of at least `MIN_TX_IX_COUNT_THRESHOLD` = 10 instructions, because wallets add compute-budget and protection steps to ordinary buys), `whale-cap` and `team-cant-buy`. Pass the launch's `guardSecs` and `openDelaySecs`: rule times count from the launch's open, and nobody can buy from the pool before the batch has run. `simulateTransfer` takes `builtin: { snipeShieldSecs, maxBuyBps, maxWalletBps, p2pLocked }` to apply the launch's own guard first, and `toImmutableOwner: false` to try a receiving account whose owner can be reassigned (refused during the guard: `MutableOwner`).

**Launch with the rules.** `planLaunch({ …, rules })` verifies the rules for the plan's guard and adds them to what the identity signs (attestation message v3 carries the rules' hash). They are published as their own record, `["rules", launch, rules_hash]`, from the throwaway payer, and must be final before the identity signs; `launch` then installs exactly those bytes in the Launch Guard's policy. The flow is the quick launch's, with `publish_rules` added and no autopilot:

```ts
import { Connection, Keypair, type Transaction } from "@solana/web3.js";
import {
  assertCluster, buildFundThrowawayPayerTx, buildMetadataDoc, buildPlannedAttestTx, buildPlannedCreateLaunchTx,
  buildPlannedLaunchTx, buildPlannedPublishRulesTx, buildPlannedPublishTx, buildSweepPayerTx, clusterUnixTime, compileRules,
  encodeIndexedPng, leafLedger, parseRules, planLaunch, pqIdentity, PRESETS, sendAndConfirm, sendAttestLaunchTx,
  sendPublishMetadataTx, sendPublishRulesTx, simulateAndExplain, throwawayPayerFunding, waitForLaunchRules,
  waitForLaunchWindow, waitForTokenMeta,
} from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const creator: Keypair;
declare const phrase: string;
declare const iconRgba: Uint8Array;
declare const ledgerStore: leafLedger.LeafLedgerStore;

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");
await assertCluster(conn, "devnet");
async function send(tx: Transaction, finalized = false): Promise<string> {
  const sim = await simulateAndExplain(conn, tx);
  if (!sim.ok || sim.unknownPrograms.length > 0) throw new Error(`refusing to sign: ${sim.error ?? "unknown programs"}`);
  tx.partialSign(creator);
  return sendAndConfirm(conn, tx, finalized ? { commitment: "finalized" } : {});
}

const secret = pqIdentity.importMaster(phrase);
const identity = await pqIdentity.deriveIdentity(secret.master, "devnet", 0);
const ledger = leafLedger.createLeafLedger(ledgerStore);

// Custom parameters: the Fair preset with a 30-minute guard. The rules are compiled for that guard.
const params = { ...PRESETS.fair.params, guardSecs: 1_800 };
const ruleText = "rules v1\nguard 30m\nalways: deny when p2p and amount > 1000 tokens code P2P\n";
const rules = compileRules(parseRules(ruleText, { guardSecs: params.guardSecs }), { guardSecs: params.guardSecs });
const doc = buildMetadataDoc({
  name: "Example B",
  symbol: "EXB",
  description: "A launch with one launch rule.",
  iconPng: await encodeIndexedPng(iconRgba, 32, 32, 16),
});

const now = await clusterUnixTime(conn);
const plan = planLaunch({
  creator: creator.publicKey,
  identity,
  params,
  recipients: [{ wallet: creator.publicKey, bps: 10_000 }], // the creator's share of the fees, to the wallet
  metadata: { name: "Example B", symbol: "EXB", doc },
  rules,
  opensAt: now + 900n,
  nowSecs: now,
});
console.log(plan.windowIso, plan.rulesExplanation);

await send((await buildPlannedCreateLaunchTx(conn, plan)).tx, true); // wait until finalized

const payer = Keypair.generate();
const funding = await throwawayPayerFunding(conn, { metadata: plan.metadata, rules: plan.rules, launch: plan.launch, lmsPublicKey: identity.publicKey });
await send((await buildFundThrowawayPayerTx(conn, creator.publicKey, payer.publicKey, { lamports: funding.lamports })).tx);

const published = await buildPlannedPublishTx(conn, plan, payer);
if (published.status === "ready") await sendPublishMetadataTx(conn, published);
await waitForTokenMeta(conn, plan.launch, plan.metadataHash);

// publish_rules: verified by the program for this launch's guard, never modified or closed afterwards.
const publishedRules = await buildPlannedPublishRulesTx(conn, plan, payer); // null for a plan without rules
if (publishedRules !== null && publishedRules.status === "ready") await sendPublishRulesTx(conn, publishedRules);
await waitForLaunchRules(conn, plan.launch, plan.rulesHash); // default: finalized

// Attestation v3: the identity signs the parameters, the record's hash, the RULES' hash and the window.
const attest = await buildPlannedAttestTx(conn, plan, { identity, ledger, payer });
if (attest.status === "ready") {
  const outcome = await sendAttestLaunchTx(conn, attest, { ledger });
  if (outcome.status !== "attested") throw new Error(`not attested (${outcome.status}): ${outcome.detail}`);
} else if (attest.status === "leaf-landed") {
  throw new Error(`leaf ${attest.leaf} already landed: confirmAttestation tells what it did`);
}
const sweep = await buildSweepPayerTx(conn, payer, creator.publicKey);
if (sweep !== null) await sendAndConfirm(conn, sweep.tx);
identity.keyPair.wipe();
pqIdentity.wipeMaster(secret);

await waitForLaunchWindow(conn, plan.launch);
const mint = Keypair.generate();
await send((await buildPlannedLaunchTx(conn, plan, creator.publicKey, mint)).tx);
```

After `launch`, the certificate (version 4) has `checks = 8,191`: the twelve required bits plus `RULES_BOUND` (4,096), and the Launch Guard's policy (`fetchHookPolicy(conn, mint)`) holds exactly the published bytes in its `rules`. `verifyLaunch` reports them in `report.rules` and `checkQsl1` in `result.programmable` (checks P.R1 to P.R4).

A rule set of at most `PUBLISH_RULES_LEGACY_MAX_BYTES` (898) bytes can also be published by any wallet in a legacy transaction (`buildPublishRulesTx(conn, payer, { launch, rules })`); the v1 form from the throwaway payer handles every size up to 1,228 bytes. A launch whose rules do not verify for its guard is refused before anything is sent (`InvalidRules`, 6048).

### The post-quantum identity

A creator identity is an RFC 8554 `LMS_SHA256_M32_H10` key over `LMOTS_SHA256_N32_W4`: **1,024 one-time leaves** under one 56-byte public key. On chain it is named `identityId = SHA256(0x21 || publicKey)` (the launch's `pq_identity`). It signs launch attestations (`attest_launch`) and autopilot approvals (`pq_authorize`). Each leaf signs **one message, ever**: a second signature at the same leaf leaks enough of that one-time key for forgeries. Everything below exists to make that impossible. Background: [docs/POST_QUANTUM.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/POST_QUANTUM.md).

Its secret comes from a 24-word phrase or a passkey, **never from a wallet**: an Ed25519 signature is deterministic, so whoever recovers the wallet key (a quantum computer, from the public address) could recompute anything derived from it.

#### The 24-word phrase

```ts
import { generateRecoveryPhrase, phraseProblems, pqIdentity } from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const typedBack: string; // the user types the words back, to prove the backup

const phrase = generateRecoveryPhrase(); // 24 BIP-39 words, 256 bits from the platform CSPRNG: show them once, offline
const problems = phraseProblems(typedBack); // e.g. an unknown word or a wrong checksum, in plain English
if (problems.length > 0) throw new Error(problems.join(" "));

const secret = pqIdentity.importMaster(typedBack); // { entropy, master }: master is the 64-byte BIP-39 seed
const backup = pqIdentity.exportMasterAsPhrase(secret); // the same 24 words, checked to restore the identical master
console.log(backup === phrase);
pqIdentity.wipeMaster(secret); // overwrite both secrets when done
```

The same phrase also derives post-quantum vault keys ([PQ vault](#pq-vault-post-quantum-custody)) through other derivation paths. Keep it apart from any wallet seed phrase.

#### Passkeys

In a browser, the identity's secret can come from a passkey instead: a discoverable credential with the WebAuthn **PRF** extension and user verification. The PRF output becomes the entropy of 24 words (`HKDF-SHA256(prf, "phalanx/pq/passkey/v1", "phalanx/pq/passkey/v1/bip39-entropy", 32)`: the domain tags keep the project's earlier name on purpose, since changing them would change every key), so a passkey identity has a 24-word backup too. The RP ID must be the exact app host, never a shared parent domain.

```ts
import { pqIdentity } from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

const rpId = location.hostname; // the exact host of your app

// Once: create the passkey. The SDK builds the options (rp id, user verification required, the PRF extension).
const creation = pqIdentity.passkeyCreationOptions({ rpId, rpName: "My app", userName: "Quantum key" });
const created = (await navigator.credentials.create({ publicKey: creation as unknown as PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions })) as PublicKeyCredential | null;
if (created === null) throw new Error("no passkey was made");
if (created.getClientExtensionResults().prf?.enabled === false) throw new Error("this passkey cannot hold a quantum key (no PRF): use 24 words");
const credentialId = new Uint8Array(created.rawId); // store it: another passkey of the site would derive another identity

// Every session: one assertion evaluates the PRF; the SDK checks the RP ID, user presence and verification, the length.
const request = pqIdentity.passkeyRequestOptions({ rpId, credentialIds: [credentialId] });
const got = (await navigator.credentials.get({ publicKey: request as unknown as PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions })) as PublicKeyCredential | null;
if (got === null) throw new Error("the passkey did not answer");
const response = got.response as AuthenticatorAssertionResponse;
const secret = pqIdentity.deriveMasterFromPasskeyAssertion(
  { authenticatorData: response.authenticatorData, clientExtensionResults: got.getClientExtensionResults() },
  { rpId },
);
const backup = pqIdentity.exportMasterAsPhrase(secret); // offer it: the 24 words that restore this passkey's identity
console.log(backup.split(" ").length);
```

The casts are there because the SDK's option objects are plain structural data, typed independently of the DOM typings (the SDK touches no browser API but the CSPRNG); the web app does the same. Feature-detect PRF support and fall back to the phrase. Lower-level pieces: `passkeyPrfFromAssertion`, `deriveMasterFromPasskeyPrf(prf, { userVerified: true })`, `passkeyEntropy`, `checkPasskeyRpId`, `passkeyPrfSalt`.

#### Deriving the identity

```ts
import { Connection } from "@solana/web3.js";
import { fetchIdentity, lms, pqIdentity, toHex } from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const phrase: string;

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");
const secret = pqIdentity.importMaster(phrase);
const treeCache = lms.memoryTreeCacheStore(); // or your durable store: { get(key), put(key, bytes) }

// Identity `index` of the phrase, for one cluster: keys differ per cluster and per index.
const identity = await pqIdentity.deriveIdentity(secret.master, "devnet", 0, {
  cache: treeCache,                                           // a valid cached tree loads in milliseconds
  onProgress: (done, total) => console.log(`${done}/${total} leaves`), // non-blocking key generation otherwise (~0.6 s in Node)
});
console.log(toHex(identity.identityId), identity.address.toBase58()); // the launch's pq_identity, and its account

// The identity account (created by its first attestation): the used-leaf bitmap, 1,024 bits.
const account = await fetchIdentity(conn, identity.publicKey);
console.log(account?.usedCount ?? 0, "leaves used on chain");
pqIdentity.wipeMaster(secret);
```

Use one identity index per purpose (`deriveIdentity(master, cluster, index)`): indexes never share leaves. A tree cache holds public data only (65,536 bytes, authenticated): cache trees only through it (`exportTreeCache`), never by hand, because a forged tree would name a forged key.

#### The leaf ledger

The identity account's on-chain bitmap records only signatures that **landed**. A signature that was simulated, sent but dropped, or signed in another tab still used its leaf. So every identity signature goes through a **leaf ledger**: a durable record in which the leaf is reserved for its message before any signature exists, and the signature is recorded before it is returned. Signing the same message again returns the recorded bytes; a leaf never signs a second message.

`leafLedger.createLeafLedger(store, { lock? })` runs on any key-value store with an **atomic** `add` (write only if the key is absent, and say whether it wrote): an exclusive file create, a SQL `INSERT` without `REPLACE`, an IndexedDB `add()`. One store can hold both the leaf ledger and the vault-key ledger (keys are namespaced). Records hold public data only. Back the store up.

In Node, one file per key, with an exclusive create:

```ts
import { mkdir, open, readdir, readFile, rename } from "node:fs/promises";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { leafLedger, type LeafLedgerStore } from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

/** One file per key. `add` is an exclusive create (the atomic add the ledger needs); every write is fsynced. */
async function fileLedgerStore(dir: string): Promise<LeafLedgerStore> {
  await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
  const file = (key: string): string => join(dir, encodeURIComponent(key));
  const write = async (path: string, value: string, flag: "wx" | "w"): Promise<void> => {
    const fh = await open(path, flag);
    try {
      await fh.writeFile(value, "utf8");
      await fh.sync();
    } finally {
      await fh.close();
    }
  };
  const code = (e: unknown): string | undefined => (e as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code;
  return {
    async get(key) {
      try {
        return await readFile(file(key), "utf8");
      } catch (e) {
        if (code(e) === "ENOENT") return null;
        throw e;
      }
    },
    async add(key, value) {
      try {
        await write(file(key), value, "wx");
        return true;
      } catch (e) {
        if (code(e) === "EEXIST") return false;
        throw e;
      }
    },
    async put(key, value) {
      const tmp = `${file(key)}.${process.pid}.tmp`;
      await write(tmp, value, "w");
      await rename(tmp, file(key));
    },
    async keys(prefix) {
      return (await readdir(dir)).filter((n) => !n.endsWith(".tmp")).map((n) => decodeURIComponent(n)).filter((k) => k.startsWith(prefix));
    },
  };
}

const ledger = leafLedger.createLeafLedger(await fileLedgerStore("./state/leaf-ledger"));
console.log(await ledger.leaves(new Uint8Array(32).fill(1))); // the leaves with a record, for an identity id
```

In a browser, IndexedDB's `add()` inside one readwrite transaction is atomic across every tab of the profile; pass a lock shared by every tab (`navigator.locks`) and ask for persistent storage, so the browser does not evict the ledger:

```ts
import { leafLedger, type LedgerLock, type LeafLedgerStore } from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

function openDb(name: string): Promise<IDBDatabase> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const req = indexedDB.open(name, 1);
    req.onupgradeneeded = () => req.result.createObjectStore("records");
    req.onsuccess = () => resolve(req.result);
    req.onerror = () => reject(req.error ?? new Error("IndexedDB open failed"));
  });
}

function idbLedgerStore(db: IDBDatabase): LeafLedgerStore {
  const run = <T>(mode: IDBTransactionMode, fn: (s: IDBObjectStore) => IDBRequest<T>): Promise<T> =>
    new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const t = mode === "readwrite" ? db.transaction("records", mode, { durability: "strict" }) : db.transaction("records", mode);
      const r = fn(t.objectStore("records"));
      t.oncomplete = () => resolve(r.result);
      t.onerror = () => reject(t.error ?? r.error);
      t.onabort = () => reject(t.error ?? r.error);
    });
  return {
    get: async (key) => {
      const v: unknown = await run("readonly", (s) => s.get(key));
      return typeof v === "string" ? v : null;
    },
    // Atomic across tabs: add() fails with ConstraintError when the key exists, and the transaction still commits.
    add: (key, value) =>
      new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
        const t = db.transaction("records", "readwrite", { durability: "strict" });
        const r = t.objectStore("records").add(value, key);
        let added = false;
        r.onsuccess = () => {
          added = true;
        };
        r.onerror = (ev) => {
          if (r.error?.name === "ConstraintError") {
            ev.preventDefault();
            ev.stopPropagation();
          }
        };
        t.oncomplete = () => resolve(added);
        t.onabort = () => reject(t.error ?? r.error);
      }),
    put: async (key, value) => {
      await run("readwrite", (s) => s.put(value, key));
    },
    keys: async (prefix) => (await run("readonly", (s) => s.getAllKeys())).filter((k): k is string => typeof k === "string" && k.startsWith(prefix)),
  };
}

// One lock for every tab: the ledger's, and the signing lock of buildPlannedAttestTx / buildPqAuthorizeTx.
const lock: LedgerLock = (name, fn) => navigator.locks.request(name, () => fn());
await navigator.storage.persist();
const ledger = leafLedger.createLeafLedger(idbLedgerStore(await openDb("my-app-ledgers")), { lock });
console.log(typeof ledger.reserve);
```

`leafLedger.storageLeafLedgerStore(localStorage)` also works, but Web Storage's `add` is atomic within one tab only, so `createLeafLedger` refuses it without a cross-tab `lock`. `leafLedger.memoryLeafLedgerStore()` and `createMemoryLeafLedger()` are for tests. The web app's IndexedDB store, with the same rules, is [`app/src/lib/ledger.ts`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/app/src/lib/ledger.ts).

#### Several devices

**Use one device per quantum key unless you import its records.** The same 24 words (or a synced passkey) give the same identity on every device, but each device's ledger only knows its own records. A message's leaf is the first leaf the ledger does not hold after a **secret** starting point (derived from the identity's seed and the message, audit round 4 ID-F1), so two devices that never share records sign two different messages at the same leaf about once in 1,024 messages, and then anyone holding both signatures can forge at that leaf. Three safe arrangements:

- one ledger per identity, shared by every device and tab (one store); or
- move the records: export on the device that signed, import on the other one **before** it signs anything with that identity; or
- one identity index per device (`deriveIdentity(master, cluster, index)`).

```ts
import { leafLedger, type LeafLedger, type PqIdentity } from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const identity: PqIdentity;
declare const ledgerHere: LeafLedger;  // the device that signed
declare const ledgerThere: LeafLedger; // the other device, before it signs

// On the device that signed: public data only (identity id, leaves, messages, signatures).
const exported = await leafLedger.exportLeafRecords(ledgerHere, identity.identityId);
const file = JSON.stringify(exported);

// On the other device. Every signature is re-verified, and nothing is written if one record fails.
const summary = await leafLedger.importLeafRecords(ledgerThere, identity.publicKey, JSON.parse(file) as leafLedger.LeafLedgerExport);
console.log(`${summary.added} added, ${summary.merged} completed, ${summary.unchanged} already known`);
if (summary.compromised.length > 0) console.warn(`leaves holding two signatures: ${summary.compromised.join(", ")}: move to a fresh identity index`);
```

An import only adds taken leaves: a record without a signature proves nothing, so it only marks its leaf taken and never re-points a message (audit round 4, ID-F2b / ID-F3). `leafLedger.launchSignatures(ledger, identityId, launch)` lists every window the identity signed for a launch, read from the signed bytes themselves. The vault has the same pair: `exportVaultKeyRecords` / `importVaultKeyRecords`.

#### When the identity refuses to sign

Since 0.9.0 (audit round 4, client fixes ID-F1 to ID-F6), the identity's signers refuse, **before anything is reserved or signed**, in these situations. Nothing is lost by stopping; each one needs a specific answer from the person, in plain words:

| Refusal | Why | The answer |
|---|---|---|
| `UnknownLeavesError` | The identity's on-chain bitmap shows used leaves this ledger never signed at: the key was used on another device or app, or this browser's data was cleared. A signature made there that has not landed is invisible here. (An RPC that lies about the bitmap gets the same answer: nothing is signed, instead of being steered onto a used leaf.) | Import the other device's records, then try again. Only for a **small** count, and only when the person confirms that every signature made elsewhere has landed, record those leaves as taken: `acknowledgeUnknownLeaves(ledger, publicKey, used, { expectedCount: e.unknownCount })` (refused if the count changed since it was shown). A large count is the sign of a lying RPC: never confirm it. |
| `ClockSkewError` | The RPC's clock and this device's (or the second RPC's) differ by more than 120 s, so a time the key signs could be one the person never chose. | Nothing to confirm: fix the device's date and time, or use another RPC (`secondConnection`). |
| `SignatureCapError` | Three earlier signatures of this launch (or of this launch and approval kind) never landed with success; each can still be landed by whoever holds it. | Land them or let them expire. One more only after the person explicitly confirms: retry with `acknowledgeExtraSignatures: true`. |
| `PendingAttestationError` | A new window is refused: an earlier signed window of this launch was never seen landing and has not ended, so it could still land and take the attestation slot. | `landOrBurnPending` (re-sends the recorded bytes, never a new signature), or wait until those windows end. Best: retire them with `burnOnly: true` while the current attestation still holds the slot. |
| `AttestRetryLimitError` | Two landings of this launch only burned their leaf (`MAX_BURN_ONLY_LANDINGS`): each new signature spends one of the 1,024 leaves. | Fix the cause in `e.reasons` (`record-missing`, `rules-missing`, `invalid-window`, `wrong-identity`, `already-attested`), then raise `maxBurnOnlyLandings` deliberately. |

The web app's handling, for the UX pattern: [`app/src/lib/signErrors.ts`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/app/src/lib/signErrors.ts) (the plain-English texts; at most 3 unknown signatures can be confirmed, by typing a sentence) and [`app/src/components/KeyUsedElsewhere.tsx`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/app/src/components/KeyUsedElsewhere.tsx) (import first; confirm only after re-reading the bitmap, on a second RPC when there is one).

```ts
import { Connection, type Keypair } from "@solana/web3.js";
import {
  acknowledgeUnknownLeaves, AttestRetryLimitError, buildPlannedAttestTx, bytesEqual, ClockSkewError, ClusterMismatchError,
  fetchIdentity, getLaunchFlowStatus, landOrBurnPending, leafLedger, PendingAttestationError, PQ_IDENTITY, SignatureCapError,
  UnknownLeavesError,
  type AttestLaunchTx, type LaunchPlan, type LeafLedger, type LedgerLock, type PqIdentity,
} from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const conn: Connection;
declare const secondConn: Connection; // another provider's RPC: the clock (and your bitmap re-read) must agree
declare const plan: LaunchPlan;
declare const identity: PqIdentity;
declare const ledger: LeafLedger;
declare const payer: Keypair;         // the funded throwaway payer
declare function askUser(question: string): Promise<boolean>; // an explicit confirmation in your UI
declare function otherDeviceExport(): Promise<leafLedger.LeafLedgerExport | null>; // a file the person brings in

const signingLock: LedgerLock = (name, fn) => navigator.locks.request(name, () => fn()); // one signer per launch, every tab
const UNKNOWN_CONFIRM_MAX = 3; // never let a person confirm more than a few unknown signatures away

async function attest(acknowledgeExtraSignatures = false): Promise<AttestLaunchTx> {
  try {
    return await buildPlannedAttestTx(conn, plan, { identity, ledger, payer, signingLock, secondConnection: secondConn, acknowledgeExtraSignatures });
  } catch (e) {
    if (e instanceof UnknownLeavesError) {
      // "This quantum key was used on another device or app." Nothing was signed.
      const exported = await otherDeviceExport();
      if (exported !== null) {
        await leafLedger.importLeafRecords(ledger, identity.publicKey, exported); // the safe answer
        return attest(acknowledgeExtraSignatures);
      }
      const confirmed = e.unknownCount <= UNKNOWN_CONFIRM_MAX && (await askUser(`${e.unknownCount} signature(s) of this key were made elsewhere. Have they ALL gone through?`));
      if (!confirmed) throw e;
      // Read the key's record again on both RPCs: they must agree (a lying RPC would show exactly such leaves).
      const empty = new Uint8Array(PQ_IDENTITY.LEAF_BITMAP_LEN);
      const [here, there] = await Promise.all([fetchIdentity(conn, identity.publicKey), fetchIdentity(secondConn, identity.publicKey)]);
      const used = here?.used ?? empty;
      if (!bytesEqual(used, there?.used ?? empty)) throw new Error("the two RPCs disagree about this key's record: import the other device's records instead");
      await acknowledgeUnknownLeaves(ledger, identity.publicKey, used, { expectedCount: e.unknownCount }); // refuses if the count changed
      return attest(acknowledgeExtraSignatures);
    }
    if (e instanceof ClockSkewError) {
      throw new Error(`Your device clock and the network disagree by ${e.skewSecs} seconds: fix your clock or try another RPC.`);
    }
    if (e instanceof SignatureCapError) {
      if (!acknowledgeExtraSignatures && (await askUser(`${e.count} earlier signatures of this launch never landed. Sign one more anyway?`))) return attest(true);
      throw e;
    }
    if (e instanceof PendingAttestationError) {
      for (const p of e.pending) console.log(`leaf ${p.leaf}: ${p.windowIso.notBefore} to ${p.windowIso.notAfter}, landing it now ${p.landingNow}`);
      // Land them with their recorded bytes (fund the payer first: fundingLamportsForPending). Or wait until they end.
      const { landings, remaining } = await landOrBurnPending(conn, { launch: plan.launch, identity, ledger, payer });
      console.log(landings.map((l) => `${l.leaf}: ${l.outcome.status}`), `${remaining.length} still pending`);
      throw e; // the launch's window may have changed: read getLaunchFlowStatus before planning anything new
    }
    if (e instanceof AttestRetryLimitError) throw new Error(`fix this before signing again: ${e.reasons.join(", ")}`);
    if (e instanceof ClusterMismatchError) throw e; // never sign against another cluster
    throw e;
  }
}

const built = await attest();
console.log(built.status, built.windowIso);

// While the current attestation holds the slot, older signatures can only burn their leaf: retire them now.
const status = await getLaunchFlowStatus(conn, plan.launch, { pending: { ledger, lmsPublicKey: identity.publicKey } });
if ((status.pendingSignatures?.length ?? 0) > 0 && (status.step === "wait-for-window" || status.step === "launch")) {
  await landOrBurnPending(conn, { launch: plan.launch, identity, ledger, payer, burnOnly: true });
}
```

`findPendingAttestations(conn, { launch, lmsPublicKey, ledger })` lists the same pending signatures on its own; `fundingLamportsForPending(conn, { launch, identity, ledger })` is what the payer needs to land them. `buildPqAuthorizeTx` (and the activation and freeze flows built on it) raise the same `UnknownLeavesError`, `ClockSkewError` and `SignatureCapError`, and take the same `signingLock`, `secondConnection` and `acknowledgeExtraSignatures` options.

### Commit, claim, swaps and fees

**The fair-open batch.** For the first minutes after `launch` (the preset's `openDelaySecs`), nobody can buy from the pool: buyers `commit` SOL to one shared batch, a keeper sends `execute_batch`, which makes the pool's first swap for everyone at the same price (pro rata above the batch's cap), and each commit is then `claim`ed. A commit names its payout owners once, on the owner's first commit: `tokenOwner` (the committer, or an opened PQ vault of the launch's mint) and `refundOwner` (the committer, or a wSOL PQ vault). There is no separate "claim to" instruction: `claim` (permissionless, anyone may send it) pays the tokens to ATA(token owner) and the unspent SOL to ATA(refund owner), so naming your post-quantum vaults at commit time is how a claim lands straight in post-quantum custody.

```ts
import { Connection, PublicKey, type Keypair } from "@solana/web3.js";
import {
  buildClaimTx, buildCommitTx, buildExecuteBatchTx, expectedBatchFill, fetchLaunch, fetchPayoutVault, masterFromPhrase,
  prepareFeeVault, preparePqVault, sendAndConfirm,
} from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const me: Keypair;
declare const launch: PublicKey;
declare const phrase: string; // the post-quantum phrase that controls your vaults

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");
const l = await fetchLaunch(conn, launch);
if (l === null) throw new Error("no such launch");

// Your vaults for the launch's mint (tokens) and for wSOL (refunds). Only an opened vault can be a payout owner.
const master = masterFromPhrase(phrase);
const tokenVault = await preparePqVault(conn, { master, cluster: "devnet", mint: l.baseMint, payer: me.publicKey });
const refundVault = await prepareFeeVault(conn, { master, cluster: "devnet", payer: me.publicKey });
master.fill(0);
for (const openTx of [tokenVault.openTx, refundVault.openTx]) {
  if (openTx === null) continue; // already open
  openTx.sign(me);
  await sendAndConfirm(conn, openTx);
}

// What the vault can still commit: commits naming one vault share one wallet's cap.
const used = (await fetchPayoutVault(conn, launch, tokenVault.vault))?.committed ?? 0n;
console.log(`room left for this vault: ${l.batchWalletCap === 0n ? "no cap" : l.batchWalletCap - used} lamports`);

// Show the expected fill next to the commit: above the total cap, commits fill pro rata and the rest is refunded.
const fill = expectedBatchFill(l, 100_000_000n);
console.log(`0.1 SOL now: about ${fill.commit.spent} spent, ${fill.commit.refund} refunded`);

const commit = await buildCommitTx(conn, me.publicKey, launch, 100_000_000n, {
  tokenOwner: tokenVault.vault,
```
