```ts
  refundOwner: refundVault.vault,
  computeUnitPrice: 50_000n,
});
commit.sign(me);
await sendAndConfirm(conn, commit);

// After the commit window: anyone executes the batch (a keeper, with a priority fee; keep it a top-level instruction).
const execute = await buildExecuteBatchTx(conn, me.publicKey, launch, { computeUnitPrice: 100_000n });
execute.sign(me);
await sendAndConfirm(conn, execute);

// After execution (or expiry, which refunds every commit in full): anyone claims a commit to its payout owners.
const claim = await buildClaimTx(conn, me.publicKey, launch, me.publicKey);
claim.sign(me);
await sendAndConfirm(conn, claim);
```

Anyone may fill a vault's batch quota by naming that vault as the token owner of their own commit (the tokens go to the vault, but the refund to their own refund owner); `buildCommitTx` refuses a commit over the vault's remaining quota, and you can then commit naming another vault or your wallet. Keepers: `buildLaunchCommitBundleV1(conn, payer, launch, baseMint, lamports)` sends `launch` and a first commit in one signed v1 transaction. Scripts: [`commit-and-claim-into-vault.ts`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/sdk/examples/commit-and-claim-into-vault.ts), [`keeper-execute-batch.ts`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/sdk/examples/keeper-execute-batch.ts).

**Swaps.** `buildSwapTx` buys or sells on the bonding curve (Meteora DBC) or, after graduation, on the DAMM v2 pool, and refuses what the Launch Guard would refuse.

```ts
import { Connection, PublicKey, type Keypair } from "@solana/web3.js";
import { buildSwapTx, getTokenBalance, sendAndConfirm, simulateAndExplain } from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const me: Keypair;
declare const mint: PublicKey;
declare const myTokenVault: PublicKey; // an opened PQ vault of this mint (preparePqVault)

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");

// Buy 0.01 SOL worth, 3% slippage at most, the tokens delivered straight into the PQ vault.
const buy = await buildSwapTx(conn, me.publicKey, mint, "buy", 10_000_000n, 300, { recipient: myTokenVault, computeUnitPrice: 20_000n });
for (const w of buy.warnings) console.warn(w); // cautions about the recipient: show them before signing
console.log(buy.quote.venue, buy.quote.expectedOut, buy.quote.minimumOut, buy.quote.feeBps, buy.quote.priceImpactBps);
const sim = await simulateAndExplain(conn, buy.tx);
if (!sim.ok) throw new Error(sim.error ?? "simulation failed");
buy.tx.sign(me);
await sendAndConfirm(conn, buy.tx);

// Sell half of what the wallet holds (sells are never blocked by the guard or by launch rules).
const held = await getTokenBalance(conn, me.publicKey, mint);
const sell = await buildSwapTx(conn, me.publicKey, mint, "sell", held / 2n, 500);
sell.tx.sign(me);
await sendAndConfirm(conn, sell.tx);
```

Slippage is at most 50% (`MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS`). While the guard is on, a buy that would break the launch's max-buy or max-wallet, or one into a token account whose owner can be reassigned (`MutableOwner`, hook error 6010), is refused before signing; every Token-2022 associated token account has a fixed owner. `recipient` refuses token accounts, mints, programs and vaults of another mint. The compute-budget options are opt-in and refused when the swap would no longer fit 1,232 bytes.

**Fees.** All permissionless (any payer). When there is nothing to claim, the builder or the program refuses (`buildClaimLpFeesTx` throws when no position has fees): treat that as "nothing to do", as the devnet scripts do.

```ts
import { Connection, PublicKey, type Keypair, type Transaction } from "@solana/web3.js";
import { buildClaimFeesTx, buildClaimLpFeesTx, buildClaimSurplusTx, buildDistributeTx, sendAndConfirm } from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const keeper: Keypair;
declare const launch: PublicKey;

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");
const send = async (tx: Transaction): Promise<string> => {
  tx.sign(keeper);
  return sendAndConfirm(conn, tx);
};

await send(await buildClaimFeesTx(conn, keeper.publicKey, launch));    // bonding-curve (DBC partner) trading fees
await send(await buildClaimSurplusTx(conn, keeper.publicKey, launch)); // DBC surplus, once the curve completed
for (const tx of await buildClaimLpFeesTx(conn, keeper.publicKey, launch)) await send(tx); // DAMM v2 LP fees, one per position
await send(await buildDistributeTx(conn, keeper.publicKey, launch));   // platform share, then the fee recipients
```

`distribute` pays the platform share to the protocol treasury, then each fee recipient at ATA(wallet, wSOL) (a wSOL PQ vault is paid into its own token account; the launch's autopilot treasury is a valid recipient), and burns the base tokens the launch authority holds. Recipients are fixed at `create_launch` and validated then (`checkFeeRecipients`): nobody can redirect them later.

### Autopilot: treasury automation

An autopilot graph (PXG1 bytes) runs a launched token's treasury inside fixed on-chain bounds: buy back and burn, burn, pay declared recipients, on a schedule, after another step, on graduation or on a condition, each step with a per-run cap, a budget and a run limit per period. **It never sells the token**, never touches the pool's locked liquidity, never mints or freezes. Anyone runs a due step for a small tip (at most 0.0001 SOL a run, a tenth of what the run moved, 0.005 SOL a day). An operator (for example an AI agent) may choose the timing and amount of its own steps, never anything outside the bounds. A graph changes only with the creator's post-quantum key and a **72-hour** public wait (`GRAPH_TIMELOCK_SECS`; a first graph may start at once), and can be frozen forever.

**Build, explain and simulate a graph** (pure):

```ts
import {
  buybackBurn, burn, compileGraph, every, explainGraph, graph, graphHashHex, graphTemplate, MIGRATION_FEE_TIERS_BPS,
  onGraduation, printGraph, simulateGraph, when,
} from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

// The quick launch's template: once a day after graduation, buy back up to 0.5 SOL and burn it, at most 3% above
// the recent low price, only with 0.5 SOL in the treasury.
const daily = graphTemplate("daily-buyback-burn", { maxIn: 0.5, premiumBps: 300, minTreasury: 0.5 });

// The same in code, plus a step that burns the treasury's tokens on graduation.
const g = graph()
  .node("buyback", every("1d"), when.graduated().and(when.treasurySolGte(0.5)), buybackBurn({ maxIn: 0.5, maxPremiumBps: 300 }), { epoch: "1d" })
  .node("burn-on-graduation", onGraduation(), null, burn({ maxTokens: 1_000_000 }))
  .build();
const bytes = compileGraph(g); // verified PXG1 bytes: what is published and approved
console.log(bytes.length, graphHashHex(bytes));

for (const line of explainGraph(daily)) console.log(line); // plain English, addresses in full
console.log(printGraph(daily)); // the autopilot text language

// What the program would allow on a market YOU describe: the pool's fee and depth are explicit.
const timeline = simulateGraph(daily, {
  epochs: 30,                              // 30 daily steps
  migrationPrice: 0.00000035,              // SOL per token: where the program's reference price starts
  poolFeeBps: MIGRATION_FEE_TIERS_BPS[2]!, // 1%: the Fair preset's graduated pool
  poolSol: 120,                            // the pool's SOL, for price impact ("none": an upper bound)
  initialTreasury: { sol: 5 },
  priceFn: (day) => 0.00000035 * (1 + 0.02 * day),
});
console.log(timeline.totals.runs, timeline.totals.burned, timeline.final.treasurySol);
for (const a of timeline.assumptions) console.log(a); // show these next to the numbers
```

Templates: `GRAPH_TEMPLATES` / `graphTemplate(id, params)`: `daily-buyback-burn`, `burn-on-graduation`, `revenue-share` and `ai-buyback` (an operator-gated buyback). Each numeric parameter has a `range` for a slider. Triggers: `every(duration)` (at least 10 minutes), `after(nodeId)`, `onGraduation()`, `whenever()` (with a condition). Actions: `buybackBurn({ maxIn, maxPremiumBps })`, `burn({ maxTokens })`, `distributeSol({ maxPerRun })` with `graph().recipient(address, share)`.

What to tell holders: show `explainGraph` of the exact bytes (what is signed or published), with addresses in full. A graph's price conditions must hold for the slow **reference price** (it starts at the migration price, rises at most 5% an hour and falls at once) and for every price observed in the last 15 to 30 minutes, the run's own observation included: "at least" on the lowest of them, "at most" on the highest, never the live price alone, so a brief spike or dip can hold a step back but never set it off (`conditionPrices`, `graphConditionOver`). The flip side: anyone willing to pay trading fees can **delay any step that waits on the price** (a burn or a payout as much as a buyback), never trigger it, with one trade across the limit, `update_price` and the trade back every 15 minutes. That costs them about 96 × 2 × the pool fee × the volume that crosses the limit per day (about 2.4 SOL a day for a 100-SOL-a-side pool, a limit about 10% from the market price and a 0.25% fee), so keep limits well away from the market price and do not make a payout that must arrive on time depend on the price alone (THREAT_MODEL R37). The check errs only toward "not now": a condition that tests the price twice with overlapping leaves, such as `when.priceGte(a).or(when.priceLte(b))` with `b >= a`, can read false while the range spans both limits, even though every single price passes; bands (`when.priceGte(a).and(when.priceLte(b))`) are exact. Buybacks are bounded by the lower of the reference and the lowest price observed in the last 15 to 30 minutes, need a price check at least a minute old, and require a minimum out priced from that bound plus the step's premium: a premium below the pool's fee (`minPremiumForFee`) never buys anything. `simulateGraph` shows what the program would allow on the market you describe; real prices, keepers and fees differ.

**Payees.** Before a graph with recipients is planned, its payees are checked like fee recipients (`checkGraphRecipients(conn, recipients)` → `{ ok, refusals, warnings, withoutAccount }`): a PQ vault of another mint (it never releases wSOL: the share would be lost), token accounts, mints, programs and off-curve addresses without an account are refused; a recipient without a wSOL account yet is skipped by the program (its share stays in the treasury) until it creates one.

**Publish, approve, activate.** The quick launch's step 6 above is the whole sequence for a first graph: `planGraphActivation` (fixes `activateAt`, which the identity signs, and checks the payees and the clocks), then `buildNextGraphActivationTx` repeatedly, which builds whatever comes next from live accounts: `buildInitAutopilotTx`, `buildPublishGraphTx` (legacy, up to `PUBLISH_GRAPH_LEGACY_MAX_BYTES` = 898 bytes, any wallet) or `buildPublishGraphV1Tx` (any size, the throwaway payer), `buildPqAuthorizeTx` (kind 1, the identity's approval over `activationPayload(autopilot, graphHash, activateAt)`), `buildActivateTx` (queues it) and, once `activateAt` came, `buildApplyPendingTx`. `getGraphActivationStatus` says where a plan stands (`stage`, `next`, `applyAtIso` and a plain line). A **replacement** graph uses the same calls: its `activateAt` is at least 72 hours after both its queuing and its approval's landing, so holders always see a change coming.

**Freeze forever.** A freeze approval names the last second it may be used (`notAfter`, default one hour, at most `FREEZE_MAX_VALID_SECS` = 24 hours after this device's clock), so an approval that was landed and then withheld cannot be used much later.

```ts
import { Connection, PublicKey, type Keypair } from "@solana/web3.js";
import {
  buildNextFreezeTx, buildPqAuthorizeTx, buildRevokeOperatorTx, planFreeze, planRevokeOperator, sendAndConfirm,
  sendPqAuthorizeTx,
  type LeafLedger, type PqIdentity,
} from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const creator: Keypair;
declare const payer: Keypair; // a funded throwaway payer (fundingLamportsForAuthorize)
declare const identity: PqIdentity;
declare const ledger: LeafLedger;
declare const launch: PublicKey;

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");

// Freeze the running graph: approve (pq_authorize, kind 2), then freeze before notAfter.
const freeze = await planFreeze(conn, launch, { validForSecs: 3_600 });
console.log(`usable until ${freeze.notAfterIso}; cancels a queued graph: ${freeze.cancelsPendingGraph}`);
for (;;) {
  const next = await buildNextFreezeTx(conn, launch, freeze, { payer: creator.publicKey, throwaway: payer, identity, ledger, creator: creator.publicKey });
  if (next === null) break; // frozen (or the plan expired or was superseded: getFreezeStatus says which)
  if (next.step === "authorize") {
    const r = next.result;
    if (r.status === "ready") {
      const outcome = await sendPqAuthorizeTx(conn, r, { ledger });
      if (outcome.status !== "authorized") throw new Error(`${outcome.status}: ${outcome.detail}`);
    } else if (r.status === "leaf-landed") throw new Error(`leaf ${r.leaf} landed without this approval`);
  } else {
    next.result.sign(creator);
    await sendAndConfirm(conn, next.result);
  }
}

// Remove the running graph's operator (allowed even after a freeze): approve kind 3, then revoke_operator.
const revoke = await planRevokeOperator(conn, launch); // the payload names the running graph's own approval (v3)
console.log(revoke.plain);
const approval = await buildPqAuthorizeTx(conn, { launch, creator: creator.publicKey, identity, ledger, kind: 3, payloadHash: revoke.payloadHash, payer });
if (approval.status === "ready") await sendPqAuthorizeTx(conn, approval, { ledger });
const revokeTx = await buildRevokeOperatorTx(conn, creator.publicKey, launch);
revokeTx.sign(creator);
await sendAndConfirm(conn, revokeTx);
```

`buildPqAuthorizeTx` signs only kinds 1 (activate), 2 (freeze) and 3 (revoke operator): the launchpad writes an `Authorization` for no other kind, and a signature of another kind would only burn its leaf. A freeze needs `freezeNotAfter` and is refused once the cluster clock is past it (`FreezeExpired`, autopilot error 6040).

**Binding.** After `launch`, anyone sends `buildBindMintTx(conn, payer, launch)` (the autopilot learns its mint, so it can burn what it buys). After graduation and migration, anyone sends `buildBindPoolTx(conn, payer, launch)` (the DAMM v2 pool; buybacks need it).

#### Keepers

Anyone may run a due step and is tipped from the treasury. The SDK keeper follows one rule that matters for the buyback's price bound: **before any buyback it makes its own price check** (`update_price`, free) and waits at least a minute (`KEEPER_OBSERVATION_WAIT_SECS` = 60 s) after it, never relying on observations others made. A buyback's protection against a manipulated pool price rests on at least one honest observation in its 15-to-30-minute window (audit round 4, A4-1), so a launch should also run an independent observer that calls `update_price` at least every `KEEPER_OBSERVER_INTERVAL_SECS` (600 s).

```ts
import { Connection, PublicKey, type Keypair } from "@solana/web3.js";
import {
  buildUpdatePriceTx, clusterUnixTime, KEEPER_OBSERVER_INTERVAL_SECS, planKeeperStep, runKeeper, sendAndConfirm,
  simulateAndExplain,
} from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const keeper: Keypair;   // pays the fees, receives the tips
declare const observer: Keypair; // an independent price observer (can be the same key)
declare const launch: PublicKey;

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");

// The whole loop: apply a due graph, check the price, wait a minute, run what is due, until idle.
const result = await runKeeper(conn, { caller: keeper, launch, maxSteps: 6, computeUnitPrice: 10_000n });
for (const s of result.steps) console.log(s.kind, s.node, s.detail, s.signature, s.costs?.totalLamports, s.expectedTipLamports);
console.log(result.stopped, result.detail, `cost ${result.costLamports} lamports`);

// Or step by step, with your own signer (simulate first, always).
let ownObservationAt: bigint | null = null;
for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
  const step = await planKeeperStep(conn, keeper.publicKey, launch, { ownObservationAt });
  if (step.kind === "idle") break;
  if (step.kind === "wait") {
    const secs = step.untilSecs - (await clusterUnixTime(conn));
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, (Math.max(0, Number(secs)) + 1) * 1_000));
    continue;
  }
  if (step.kind === "update-price" && step.because === "own-check-not-seen") break; // the program never saw our check: stop
  const sim = await simulateAndExplain(conn, step.tx);
  if (!sim.ok) throw new Error(sim.error ?? "simulation failed");
  step.tx.sign(keeper);
  await sendAndConfirm(conn, step.tx);
  if (step.kind === "update-price") ownObservationAt = await clusterUnixTime(conn); // when OUR observation landed
  if (step.kind === "run") console.log(`ran step ${step.node}, expected tip ${step.expectedTipLamports}, cost ${step.costs.totalLamports}`);
}

// An independent observer: one honest price check in every 15-minute bucket.
setInterval(async () => {
  const tx = await buildUpdatePriceTx(conn, observer.publicKey, launch);
  tx.sign(observer);
  await sendAndConfirm(conn, tx);
}, KEEPER_OBSERVER_INTERVAL_SECS * 1_000);
```

What a keeper should know:

- **Costs.** Every step states what it costs the keeper (`costs`: signature fee, priority fee, rent) and a run what it should earn (`expectedTipLamports`, an estimate from the program's tip rules: at most 100,000 lamports, 10% of what the run moved, nothing for a burn before graduation).
- **Partial buybacks.** When the pool cannot fill a step's whole amount, the keeper buys back less (at least 1% of the pool's SOL); the step stays due for the rest, and the partial run earns its share of one tip.
- **Recipients' accounts.** `buildRunTx` never creates a recipient's wSOL account (only the keeper's own tip account): a recipient without one is skipped and its share stays in the treasury; a distribution nobody can receive is refused (`NoRecipientAccount`, autopilot error 6042). A creator or recipient who wants to pay for those accounts uses `buildCreateRunAccountsTx(conn, payer, launch, { recipients: true })`.
- **Operator steps.** An operator-only step needs the operator's signature and amount: `buildRunTx(conn, operator, launch, node, { operator, amount })`; keepers skip them. The creator can remove the operator at any time, even after freezing.
- **The keeper's view.** `fetchDueNodes(conn, launch)` returns every node's status (`statuses`, `due`, `applyPendingFirst`), decided by the program's own logic; `decodeAutopilotEvent` reads `NodeRan` events (`partial`, `skipped`, `kept`, `paid`, `skippedRecipients`) from a run's logs.

An LLM-free keeper built on the Noised MCP server: [`packages/noised-mcp/examples/langgraph-operator/src/keeper.ts`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/packages/noised-mcp/examples/langgraph-operator/src/keeper.ts).

### PQ vault: post-quantum custody

A vault lives at `["vault", mint, genesis_key_id]` forever. Every withdrawal is signed by the vault's **current** LM-OTS one-time key, reserves `min(maxAmount, available)` in a payout account and rotates the key in place (the next key is `sequence + 1`); delivery is separate: `release` (by anyone) pays the recipient's canonical token account, `release_to` (signed by the recipient) pays any token account of the mint. A recipient can delay only its own payout, never the withdrawal. Each vault key signs exactly one withdrawal.

**Open and deposit:**

```ts
import { Connection, PublicKey, type Keypair, type Transaction } from "@solana/web3.js";
import { buildDepositTx, checkVaultMint, fetchVault, masterFromPhrase, preparePqVault, sendAndConfirm } from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const me: Keypair;
declare const mint: PublicKey;
declare const phrase: string; // the 24-word post-quantum phrase (generateRecoveryPhrase)

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");
const send = async (tx: Transaction): Promise<string> => {
  tx.sign(me);
  return sendAndConfirm(conn, tx);
};

// Can this mint be vaulted? Refusals block; warnings (freeze authority, transfer hook...) can delay payouts.
const eligibility = await checkVaultMint(conn, mint);
if (!eligibility.eligible) throw new Error(eligibility.refusals.join(" "));
for (const w of eligibility.warnings) console.warn(w);

// The phrase's vault account 0 for this mint (checks the RPC's cluster), and its open_vault transaction if needed.
const master = masterFromPhrase(phrase);
const target = await preparePqVault(conn, { master, cluster: "devnet", mint, payer: me.publicKey, account: 0 });
master.fill(0);
if (target.openTx !== null) await send(target.openTx);

// Deposit into the vault's own token account. SOL or another mint sent to the vault ADDRESS itself is unrecoverable.
await send(await buildDepositTx(conn, me.publicKey, mint, target.vault, 1_000_000n));
const info = await fetchVault(conn, target.vault);
console.log(info?.sequence, info?.balance, info?.reserved, info?.available, info?.tokenAccount.toBase58());
```

`buildOpenVaultTx(conn, payer, mint, genesisPk)` is the lower-level form (`genesisPk` = `deriveVaultKey(master, cluster, mint, account, 0).pk`).

**Withdraw.** `prepareWithdrawal` does the safe order in one call: the recipient confirmation, the cluster check, the vault-key ledger (a key recorded for another withdrawal throws `VaultKeyInUseError` with that withdrawal to re-broadcast), a search of the vault's history (a withdrawal the key already signed is returned to re-broadcast, nothing new is signed), the recipient check again, then the key is reserved in the ledger, signs once (deterministically) and the signature is recorded before it is returned.

```ts
import { Connection, Keypair, PublicKey } from "@solana/web3.js";
import {
  buildFundFeePayerTx, buildRefundFeePayerTx, buildReleaseTx, buildWithdrawTxWithFallback, checkRecipient, createVaultKeyLedger,
  deriveVaultKey, IncompleteSearchError, masterFromPhrase, prepareWithdrawal, RecipientConfirmationError, sendAndConfirm,
  vaultAddress, VaultKeyInUseError,
  type LeafLedgerStore, type PendingWithdrawalContinuation, type RecipientCheck, type RecipientConfirmation, type WithdrawTxArgs,
} from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const me: Keypair;               // the connected wallet (its own token accounts are refused as recipients)
declare const mint: PublicKey;
declare const destinationOwner: PublicKey; // the recipient WALLET
declare const phrase: string;
declare const store: LeafLedgerStore;    // durable, atomic add, shared by every tab and device holding the phrase
declare function askUser(check: RecipientCheck): Promise<RecipientConfirmation["acknowledged"]>; // three separate confirmations

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");
const ledger = createVaultKeyLedger(store); // one record per one-time key, written before its signature exists
const master = masterFromPhrase(phrase);
let args: WithdrawTxArgs | null = null;
try {
  // 1. Check the recipient of this exact withdrawal and show the result: refusals stop; each kind of caution is confirmed.
  const vault = vaultAddress(mint, deriveVaultKey(master, "devnet", mint, 0, 0).keyId);
  const recipient = await checkRecipient(conn, destinationOwner, mint, vault, { wallet: me.publicKey });
  if (!recipient.ok) throw new Error(recipient.refusals.join(" "));
  const confirm: RecipientConfirmation = { recipient, acknowledged: await askUser(recipient) };

  // 2. Sign once. A long history is searched in pieces: continue it, never skip it.
  let continueFrom: PendingWithdrawalContinuation | undefined;
  while (args === null) {
    try {
      const prepared = await prepareWithdrawal(conn, master, "devnet", mint, 0, { destinationOwner, maxAmount: 1_000_000n }, { ledger, confirm, continueFrom });
      const p = prepared.pending; // the key already signed a withdrawal: re-broadcast THAT one, nothing new was signed
      if (p !== null) {
        if (p.nextKey === null || !p.executable) throw new Error(`the key already signed a withdrawal that cannot execute (${p.txSignature}): do not sign again`);
        args = { mint: p.mint, vault: p.vault, sequence: p.sequence, destinationOwner: p.destinationOwner, maxAmount: p.maxAmount, signature: p.signature, nextKey: p.nextKey, nextKeyId: p.nextKeyId };
      } else if (prepared.signed !== null) {
        args = prepared.signed.args; // signed now, or the ledger's recorded signature (prepared.signed.reused)
      } else throw new Error("nothing was signed");
    } catch (e) {
      if (e instanceof IncompleteSearchError && e.search.continuation !== null) {
        continueFrom = e.search.continuation;
        continue;
      }
      if (e instanceof VaultKeyInUseError && e.withdrawal !== null) {
        args = e.withdrawal; // the key already belongs to another withdrawal: broadcast that one
        continue;
      }
      if (e instanceof RecipientConfirmationError) console.error(e.reason, e.current); // show the check again and ask
      throw e;
    }
  }
} finally {
  master.fill(0);
}

// 3. A throwaway fee payer with no authority over the vault (keep its key until it is refunded).
const feePayer = Keypair.generate();
const fund = await buildFundFeePayerTx(conn, me.publicKey, feePayer.publicKey); // 0.01 SOL by default
fund.sign(me);
await sendAndConfirm(conn, fund);

// 4. Withdraw + release in one v1 transaction when that works now, else the withdrawal alone with the SAME signature.
//    It simulates (reveals) only a signature the ledger holds.
const built = await buildWithdrawTxWithFallback(conn, feePayer, args, { ledger });
if (!built.simulation.ok) throw new Error(`${built.simulation.error}: rebuild later from the same recorded signature`);
await sendAndConfirm(conn, built.tx, { lastValidBlockHeight: built.lastValidBlockHeight });

// 5. Deliver later if release did not fit, then return what is left on the fee payer.
if (!built.includesRelease) {
  console.log(`payout ${built.payout.toBase58()} reserved, not delivered: ${built.releaseError}`);
  const release = await buildReleaseTx(conn, me.publicKey, { vault: args.vault, mint, sequence: args.sequence });
  release.sign(me);
  await sendAndConfirm(conn, release);
}
await sendAndConfirm(conn, await buildRefundFeePayerTx(conn, feePayer, me.publicKey)); // signed by the fee payer
```

If the send is dropped or expires, rebuild from the recorded signature (`buildWithdrawTxWithFallback` again, any fresh fee payer, new blockhash) and send again: a correct signature for the current sequence always executes. When the recipient's canonical account cannot receive (frozen, confidential-only), the recipient signs `buildReleaseToTx(conn, recipient, { vault, mint, sequence, destination })` to any token account of the mint; while a Launch Guard is on, `release_to` refuses a destination whose owner can be reassigned. Unreleased payouts: `listPayouts(conn, vault)`, `fetchPayout(conn, vault, sequence)`. The full script, with the ledger on disk, the confirmation flags and the fee-payer refund: [`vault-withdraw.ts`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/sdk/examples/vault-withdraw.ts).

**Several devices, and recovery.** Every device holding the phrase derives every vault key, but a ledger knows only its own records. For each vault account, either share one ledger between all devices, or import the other device's records before signing, or give each device its own vault accounts:

```ts
import { Connection, PublicKey } from "@solana/web3.js";
import {
  completeVaultKeyRecords, exportVaultKeyRecords, findPendingWithdrawal, importVaultKeyRecords, masterFromPhrase, scanVaults,
  type VaultKeyLedger, type VaultKeyLedgerExport,
} from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const ledgerHere: VaultKeyLedger;  // the device that signed
declare const ledgerThere: VaultKeyLedger; // the other device, before it signs
declare const mint: PublicKey;
declare const phrase: string;

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");

// Export the signed records (records of an old SDK get their key first, so they can be exported), import them there.
const master = masterFromPhrase(phrase);
await completeVaultKeyRecords(ledgerHere, master, "devnet", mint, 4); // vault accounts 0..=4 of this mint
const exported = JSON.stringify(await exportVaultKeyRecords(ledgerHere));
const summary = await importVaultKeyRecords(ledgerThere, JSON.parse(exported) as VaultKeyLedgerExport);
if (summary.compromised.length > 0) console.warn(`keys holding two signatures: broadcast one of the two withdrawals NOW: ${summary.compromised.join(", ")}`);
if (summary.unverifiable.length > 0) throw new Error("the other device signed with keys it could not export: do not sign here yet");

// Recovery from the 24 words alone: find the phrase's vaults for a mint, and any withdrawal already revealed.
for (const v of await scanVaults(conn, master, "devnet", mint, 4)) {
  if (!v.opened) continue;
  console.log(v.account, v.vault.toBase58(), v.sequence, v.available, v.pendingPayouts.length, v.keyMatches);
  let search = await findPendingWithdrawal(conn, v.vault);
  while (!search.complete && search.continuation !== null) search = await findPendingWithdrawal(conn, v.vault, { continueFrom: search.continuation });
  if (search.pending !== null) console.log(`a revealed withdrawal of ${search.pending.maxAmount} to ${search.pending.destinationOwner.toBase58()}: re-broadcast it`);
}
master.fill(0);
```

An import is authenticated (each signature must verify under its recorded key over its recorded withdrawal; nothing is written if one record fails) and only adds. `recordPendingWithdrawal(ledger, search)` records a found withdrawal so the fallback builder can re-broadcast it (`prepareWithdrawal` does this on its own). A search that cannot complete on this RPC (`incompleteReason: "history"`) needs an RPC that keeps the full history: never sign while it is incomplete.

### Shield: private balances

> **Mainnet only.** The shield program is deployed on mainnet (since 2026-10-13, upgradeable; [docs/MAINNET.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/MAINNET.md)) but not on devnet ([docs/DEVNET.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/DEVNET.md)), so on devnet the transactions below cannot land.

The shield wraps a token 1:1 into its **zToken**, a Token-2022 mint with confidential balances, and unwraps it again. It hides **amounts**, not parties (who sends to whom stays public), and its encryption (twisted ElGamal and zero-knowledge proofs over Curve25519) is **not** post-quantum: amounts hidden today may become public later, and the ElGamal key is derived from a signature of your Ed25519 wallet ([docs/PRIVACY.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/PRIVACY.md)). Confidential transfers themselves need zero-knowledge proofs that this SDK does not generate: use the `spl-token` CLI (5.6 or later, `--confidential`) for configure, deposit, apply-pending-balance, transfer and withdraw.

```ts
import { Connection, PublicKey, type Keypair } from "@solana/web3.js";
import { buildCreateShieldTx, buildUnwrapTx, buildWrapTx, fetchShield, sendAndConfirm, shieldAddresses, shieldMintPolicy } from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const me: Keypair;
declare const baseMint: PublicKey;

const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");

// Would create_shield accept this mint? (allowlisted extensions only: metadata pointer and metadata, transfer hook, transfer fee)
const info = await conn.getAccountInfo(baseMint);
const policy = shieldMintPolicy(info === null ? null : { address: baseMint, owner: info.owner, lamports: info.lamports, executable: info.executable, data: new Uint8Array(info.data) });
console.log(policy.eligible, policy.refusals);

const { shield, zMint, escrow } = shieldAddresses(baseMint); // the token program defaults to Token-2022
console.log(shield.toBase58(), zMint.toBase58(), escrow.toBase58());

if ((await fetchShield(conn, baseMint)) === null) {
  const create = await buildCreateShieldTx(conn, me.publicKey, baseMint); // once per base mint, by anyone
  create.sign(me);
  await sendAndConfirm(conn, create);
}
const wrap = await buildWrapTx(conn, me.publicKey, baseMint, 1_000_000n); // base tokens -> escrow, zTokens -> you
wrap.sign(me);
await sendAndConfirm(conn, wrap);
const unwrap = await buildUnwrapTx(conn, me.publicKey, baseMint, 1_000_000n); // zTokens back -> base tokens
unwrap.sign(me);
await sendAndConfirm(conn, unwrap);
```

During a Launch Guard, the shield's escrow and each recipient's associated token account count against one max-wallet, and launch rules never apply to holders moving tokens through the shield directly (the built-in guard still does).

## Errors

### Typed errors

Every refusal a UI must handle is a class you can test with `instanceof`. All are exported from the package root, except the two leaf-ledger classes (namespace `leafLedger`) and the programmable module's `ProgError` / `DslError` (root and `@noisedlabs/sdk/programmable`). Unless noted, **nothing was signed, reserved or sent** when one is thrown.

| Error (fields) | Thrown by | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ClusterMismatchError` (`expected`, `genesisHash`, `actual`) | `assertCluster`, and every post-quantum signing path that checks the cluster (`buildAttestLaunchTx`, `buildPqAuthorizeTx`, `prepareWithdrawal`, `signWithdrawal`, `preparePqVault`, `landOrBurnPending`, …) | The RPC does not serve the cluster the keys are for (by genesis hash), the hash could not be read, or localnet without `allowLocalnet`. | Use an RPC of the right cluster. Never "fix" it by changing the cluster label. |
| `ClockSkewError` (`localSecs`, `clusterSecs`, `secondClusterSecs`, `skewSecs`, `maxSkewSecs`) | `checkClockSkew`; `buildAttestLaunchTx`, `buildPlannedAttestTx`; `buildPqAuthorizeTx` kinds 1 and 2; `planGraphActivation`, `planFreeze` and the flows built on them | The cluster clock and this device's (or a second RPC's) differ by more than 120 s. | Fix the device's date and time, or use another RPC. There is nothing to confirm. |
| `UnknownLeavesError` (`identityId`, `unknownLeaves`, `unknownCount`, `usedOnChain`, `knownToLedger`, `chosenLeaf`, `chosenLeafSetOnChain`) | the identity signers: `buildAttestLaunchTx`, `buildPlannedAttestTx`, `buildPqAuthorizeTx` and their flows; `leafLedger.selectLeaf`, `leafLedger.signAtNextLeaf` | "This quantum key was used elsewhere": the bitmap shows used leaves this ledger never signed at. | Import the other device's records (`leafLedger.importLeafRecords`) and retry. For a small count only, after the person confirms every signature elsewhere has landed: `acknowledgeUnknownLeaves(…, { expectedCount: e.unknownCount })`. Never confirm a large count. |
| `SignatureCapError` (`launch`, `what`, `leaves`, `count`, `max`) | `buildAttestLaunchTx`, `buildPlannedAttestTx`, `buildPqAuthorizeTx` and their flows | `MAX_UNLANDED_SIGNATURES` (3) signatures of this launch (or launch and kind) never landed with success. | Land them (`landOrBurnPending` for attestations) or let them expire; or retry with `acknowledgeExtraSignatures: true` after an explicit confirmation. |
| `PendingAttestationError` (`launch`, `pending`) | `buildAttestLaunchTx`, `buildPlannedAttestTx` | A new window is refused: an earlier signed window of this launch was never seen landing and has not ended. | `landOrBurnPending` (fund with `fundingLamportsForPending`), or wait until the windows in `pending` end. |
| `AttestRetryLimitError` (`launch`, `landings`, `reasons`) | `buildAttestLaunchTx`, `buildPlannedAttestTx` | `MAX_BURN_ONLY_LANDINGS` (2) landings of this launch only burned their leaf. | Fix the cause (`reasons`), then raise `maxBurnOnlyLandings` deliberately. |
| `AttestPayerFundingError` (`balance`, `required`) | `sendAttestLaunchTx` | The throwaway payer cannot pay, or would be left below the rent-exempt minimum. Nothing was broadcast. | Fund the payer with the difference and send the same built transaction. |
| `PublishPayerFundingError` (`balance`, `required`) | `sendPublishMetadataTx` | The same, for `publish_metadata`. | The same. |
| `AuthorizePayerFundingError` (`balance`, `required`) | `sendPqAuthorizeTx` | The same, for `pq_authorize`. | The same (`fundingLamportsForAuthorize`). |
| `RecipientConfirmationError` (`reason`, `current`) | `prepareWithdrawal`, `signWithdrawal` | The recipient was not confirmed for this exact withdrawal: `reason` is `missing`, `mismatch` (a check of another recipient, mint or vault), `refused`, `unacknowledged` or `stale` (the check re-run before signing found a caution the user was not shown). | Show `checkRecipient`'s result (for `stale`, `current`) and ask again. |
| `VaultKeyInUseError` (`record`, `withdrawal`) | `prepareWithdrawal`, `signWithdrawal` | The vault's current key is already reserved or signed for another withdrawal in this ledger. | Re-broadcast `withdrawal` (`buildWithdrawTxWithFallback`); when it is null, prepare that same withdrawal to finish it. |
| `IncompleteSearchError` (`search`) | `prepareWithdrawal` | The history search could not rule out an already revealed signature of the current key. | Call again with `continueFrom: e.search.continuation`; when that is null, use an RPC that keeps the full history. |
| `VaultLedgerError` | the vault-key ledger, `buildWithdrawTxWithFallback`, `importVaultKeyRecords`, `prepareWithdrawal` | A record is missing, unreadable or fails authentication, a transition breaks the one-signature rule, or the ledger does not hold the signature about to be simulated. | Sign only through `prepareWithdrawal` / `signWithdrawal` with this ledger; never edit records by hand. |
| `leafLedger.LeafConflictError` | `leafLedger.reserveAndSign`, `leafLedger.signAtNextLeaf` | The leaf belongs to another message, or this process already signed another message at it. | Never force a leaf: use `selectLeaf` / `signAtNextLeaf`, and re-broadcast recorded signatures. |
| `leafLedger.LeafLedgerError` | the leaf ledger, `acknowledgeUnknownLeaves`, `importLeafRecords` | A record is missing or malformed, a transition breaks the rule, the identity is out of leaves, an import is not authentic, or the unknown-leaf count changed since it was shown. | Read the message; for a changed count, show the new count and ask again; for an exhausted identity, use the next index. |
| `MintParseError` | `parseMint`, `parseTokenAccount` and the strict Token-2022 parsers | The account is not a mint or token account these parsers accept (unknown extension types are refused). | Treat the mint as unsupported. |
| `PngError` | `pngInfo` | The bytes are not a well-formed PNG. | Ask for another icon. |
| `ProgError` (`code`, `at`) | the rules and graph builders, `compileRules`, `compileGraph`, the encoders, templates, `simulateTransfer` | The model is invalid: `code` is a verifier name of `crates/noised-rules` (`VERIFY_ERRORS`) or a model code (`UnknownKey`, `BadAmount`, …); `at.rule` / `at.node` / `at.key` point at it. | Show the message at `at`. |
| `DslError` (`line`, `col`, `offset`, `length`, `hint`, `pretty`) | `parseRules`, `parseGraph` (`tryParseRules` / `tryParseGraph` return them all) | A text-language error with its position. | Underline `offset`..`offset + length` in the editor. |

### Program errors

Error codes of the Noised programs, from their IDLs (`@noisedlabs/sdk/idl/<name>.json`):

| Program | Codes | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| `noised_launchpad` | 6000..6048 | 6016 / 6045 / 6046 / 6047 (metadata record), 6041 `PqLeafUsed`, 6048 `InvalidRules` |
| `noised_hook` (Launch Guard) | 6000..6012 | 6000 `SnipeShield`, 6001 `TransfersLocked`, 6002 `MaxBuy`, 6003 `MaxWallet`, 6010 `MutableOwner`, 6011 `RuleDenied`, 6012 `InvalidRules` |
| `noised_autopilot` | 6000..6042 | 6040 `FreezeExpired`, 6041 `RemainderTooSmall`, 6042 `NoRecipientAccount` |
| `noised_vault` | 6000..6006 | 6000 `KeyIdMismatch`, 6001 `InvalidSignature`, 6002 `InvalidNextKey`, 6003 `UnsupportedMint`, 6004 `InvalidDestination`, 6005 `MathOverflow`, 6006 `InvalidKeyIndex` |
| `noised_shield` | 6000..6009 | 6000 `UnsupportedExtension` |

The SDK maps them, and Meteora DBC and DAMM v2, Anchor and SPL Token errors, to names and messages:

```ts
import { Connection, type Transaction } from "@solana/web3.js";
import { customErrorCode, explainProgramError, plainErrorMessage, PROGRAM_IDS, sendAndConfirm, simulateAndExplain } from "@noisedlabs/sdk";

declare const tx: Transaction;
const conn = new Connection("https://api.devnet.solana.com", "confirmed");

// Before signing: what would fail, in which instruction and program, with the logs.
const sim = await simulateAndExplain(conn, tx);
if (!sim.ok) console.log(sim.error, sim.errorCode, sim.failedInstruction, sim.logs.slice(-5));

// After a failed send: the custom code it carries, then its name and a sentence for a person.
try {
  await sendAndConfirm(conn, tx);
} catch (e) {
  const code = customErrorCode(e); // null when the error carries none
  if (code !== null) {
    const known = explainProgramError(PROGRAM_IDS.hook.toBase58(), code); // takes the program id as a base58 string
    console.log(known?.name, known?.message, plainErrorMessage(PROGRAM_IDS.hook, code));
    // 6011: "RuleDenied" - "A launch rule set by the creator blocks this transfer right now. ..."
  }
}
```

`plain` (from `explainProgramError`, or `plainErrorMessage(programId, code)`, `PLAIN_ERROR_MESSAGES`) is a sentence to show a person; today it exists for the launch-rule errors (hook 6011 and 6012, launchpad 6048) and the autopilot's 6040 to 6042. `explainTransactionError(err, logs)` turns a transaction error and its logs into `{ error, errorCode }`. `customErrorCode` reads a code from an error's `logs`, from its message (`"Custom": 6011` or `custom program error: 0x177b`) and from its `cause` chain; an error that carries none of them gives `null`. The devnet test run saw a refused transaction sent without preflight reject with a plain object rather than an `Error`: keep the transaction's signature before sending, and when the error says nothing, read the landed transaction (`conn.getTransaction(signature)`) and pass its `meta.err` and `meta.logMessages` to `explainTransactionError`.

## Security notes for integrators

The client-side fixes of audit round 4 (ID-F1 to ID-F6 for identity signing, C1, C2 and M4 for custody and keepers) are in **0.9.0**: the secret leaf probe and `UnknownLeavesError` (ID-F1), authenticated imports (ID-F2b, ID-F3), the per-launch signing lock (ID-F4), the cap on unlanded signatures (ID-F2), the reviewed-message check before signing (ID-F6), and the clock checks with absolute dates (ID-F1b, ID-F5). Earlier versions lack them: do not sign with an identity through an SDK older than 0.9.0. Details: [docs/AUDIT.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/AUDIT.md) §16.

**Verify before you trust.**
- Show `verifyLaunch` to users before they buy, and treat `overall: "fail"` as "not a safe Noised launch". A mint without a launchpad-owned certificate at `["certificate", mint]` is not a Noised launch at all.
- Show a QSL-1 badge only from `qslBadge(await checkQsl1(conn, mint))`, never from the certificate's flags: keep the mint address next to it, let it open the full list of checks and `trusted`, show a candidate only where `badge.showOnTradeScreen` allows it (a cluster known not to be mainnet; never when the cluster is `unknown`) or in developer views, and re-check after a graduation, a migration or a Meteora or Token-2022 deploy. Never call a token "quantum-proof", "audited" or "verified" (QSL-1 Appendix A.3).
- Never present "programmable" as safer: show `badge.programmable.text` next to the level with its "read its rules" link and its warnings, never as a level or a better badge.
- The report is only as honest as the RPC that served it. For large decisions, run it against two independent providers and compare.
- `warn` is meaningful: the programs are upgradeable until finalized, and any change to Meteora's DBC or DAMM v2 code or upgrade authority since the reviewed slot is flagged. When Meteora deploys, review the change, then update `TRUST_ANCHORS`.
- Meteora's operators and multisig, the Token-2022 multisig and validators remain trusted (`trustedParties`); disclose them.
- Show a launch's post-quantum origin (identity, leaf, window) only from `report.pqOrigin` with `verified` true, never from the certificate, the Launch account or an event alone. A failed `pq.origin` means "not PQ-attested", whatever else passes. A graduated pool's default dynamic fee is part of its fee: quote the maximum per trade, not only the tier.

**On-chain text is untrusted.** A token's name, symbol, description, icon and links are chosen by its creator, and anyone may publish junk records under any launch.
- Show them only from a verified record (`report.metadata.verified`, or `verifyAttestation` before launch), read through its attestation or certificate, never from a record found by searching a launch's records.
- Render names, symbols, descriptions and links **as text only**: never as HTML or Markdown, never inside a URL you build, never auto-linked. Show a link with its host spelled out (`links[i].host`) and never open it automatically. Render the icon only as an `<img>` of its `data:image/png` uri. Nothing in a record is ever fetched by the SDK.
- The same applies to rule and graph labels (a label is only what the creator typed: show `explainRules` / `explainGraph`, with addresses in full) and to every string an RPC returns (error texts, logs).

**The Launch Guard has limits** (audit round 3, F2 and F4). During the guard it stops wallet-to-wallet token transfers (when the launch locks them) and, by refusing transfers (other than sells) into token accounts whose owner can be reassigned (`MutableOwner`, 6010), consolidation by reassigning an account's owner. It does not stop control of a position changing with no token transfer, which no hook can see: a wallet several people control (a multisig, a smart wallet's members, a shared key); a token account owned by a PDA or a smart wallet whose own program hands control to someone else; a PQ vault whose holder signs `withdraw` with `max_amount = 0` (a pure key rotation) and `next_key` set to another party's key; and a delegate approval (`Approve`), which lets the delegate sell during the guard. Sells are always allowed.

**Simulate before you sign.**
- Run `simulateAndExplain` on every transaction before asking a wallet to sign it. Refuse to sign if `unknownPrograms` is not empty, if the signers or writable accounts are not what the user expects, or if the size exceeds the limit.
- Builders refuse what the programs would refuse deterministically (invalid parameters, caps, vault sequence, recipients' accounts, guard rules); time windows and balances are left to simulation.
- Show the expected batch fill (`expectedBatchFill`) next to a commit: above the total cap a commit is filled pro rata and the rest refunded at claim.
- Do not modify a transaction after `buildLaunchTx` (the mint keypair already signed it) or after `buildRefundFeePayerTx` / `buildSweepPayerTx` (the payer already signed it).

**Never sign twice with a one-time post-quantum key.**
- An LM-OTS key, and each of the 1,024 leaves of an LMS identity, signs one message, ever. A second signature with the same key (another recipient, amount, next key, launch or window, or the same message with another randomizer) leaks enough of the key for forgeries. The SDK's randomizer is deterministic: signing the identical message again reproduces the identical signature; anything else is a second signature.
- **Ledgers.** Every identity signature goes through a leaf ledger and every vault signature through a vault-key ledger, on a durable store with an atomic `add`, backed up. The key is reserved before any signature exists and the signature is recorded before it is returned; re-broadcast recorded signatures instead of signing again. In a browser, pass a cross-tab lock (`navigator.locks`) to the ledgers and as `signingLock`.
- **Several devices.** One device per quantum key unless you import its records. For vaults: share one ledger, or import the other device's records before signing, or give each device its own vault accounts. A `compromised` key in an import summary holds two signatures: broadcast one of the two withdrawals at once. An `unverifiable` key is one the other device signed with but could not export: do not sign on this device until it has run `completeVaultKeyRecords` and you imported its new export.
- **Vault history.** Before signing for a vault's current sequence, search its history (`prepareWithdrawal` does): a revealed signature, even in a failed transaction, must be re-broadcast, not replaced. Never sign while the search is incomplete; continue it or use an RPC that keeps the full history. Junk transactions naming a vault are read last, so they never delay re-broadcasting a withdrawal already attempted.
- **Recipients.** The vault signers refuse to sign without the user's confirmation of `checkRecipient` for this exact recipient, mint and vault: a token account, a mint, a vault or a payout address as recipient loses the payout. Pass the connected `wallet` to `checkRecipient`, show its `refusals` (never sign then), and ask for `recipientWarnings`, `mintWarnings` and `offCurveConfirmation` as three separate confirmations.
- **Identities: clocks, one signer, a cap.** Show the absolute dates the SDK returns (`windowIso`, `activateAtIso`, `notAfterIso`), pass `secondConnection` when you have a second provider, keep a plan's `messageHash` with it (`buildPlannedAttestTx` refuses a plan whose message changed), and ask for an explicit confirmation before `acknowledgeExtraSignatures` or `acknowledgeUnknownLeaves`.
- **Attestations.** Sign only a finalized launch your wallet created, with the parameters you reviewed (`expectedParamsHash`, required; `planLaunch` fixes it), a metadata record (and rules record) that is published and finalized, and a window the cluster clock allows with 60 s to spare: anything else lands only to burn a leaf. After landing, check the attestation (`confirmAttestation`) instead of assuming it attested.
- **Cluster check.** Sign only against the cluster the keys are for. Vault and launch addresses are the same on every cluster, so a mislabeled devnet run would otherwise sign with mainnet keys, and a leaf used on one cluster is still clear on another.
- **Secrets.** The post-quantum phrase (or passkey) is separate from any wallet and is the only way to the funds and the identity. Keep `master` and `skSeed` in memory only and wipe them after use (`pqIdentity.wipeMaster`, `master.fill(0)`, `LmsKeyPair.wipe()`). Do not mutate `master` while a call that takes it runs: `prepareWithdrawal` then signs nothing, and an all-zero master is refused everywhere.
- **Fee payers.** Vault withdrawals, metadata and rules records, attestations and approvals are paid by a throwaway key with no authority: fund it, keep its key until it is swept, and return what is left. Run `checkVaultMint` before opening a vault and show its warnings.

## Browser and Node notes

| Topic | Browser | Node |
|---|---|---|
| Ledger store | IndexedDB, with `add()` in one readwrite transaction (atomic across tabs; [example](#the-leaf-ledger)); or Web Storage with a cross-tab lock. Call `navigator.storage.persist()`: evicted site data is a lost ledger. | One file per key with an exclusive create (`open(path, "wx")`), fsynced ([example](#the-leaf-ledger)); or a SQL table with a unique key. |
| Locks | Pass `lock: (name, fn) => navigator.locks.request(name, () => fn())` to `createLeafLedger` / `createVaultKeyLedger`, and the same function as `signingLock`. Without the Web Locks API, do not sign. | The default in-process mutex serializes one process. Do not run two processes on one ledger store unless the store's `add` is atomic across them (an exclusive file create is). |
| Randomness | `crypto.getRandomValues`. | `globalThis.crypto` (Node 22). |
| `buffer` | The SDK imports the `buffer` package itself: no polyfill needed. | Native. |
| Icons | `encodeIndexedPng` uses `CompressionStream("deflate")` when present and smaller; pass `{ compression: "store" }` for identical bytes on every platform. | The same (`CompressionStream` is global in Node 22). |
| Passkeys | WebAuthn PRF with user verification; the RP ID is the exact host. | Not available: use the 24-word phrase. |

- **Plain Node and Meteora.** `@coral-xyz/anchor` exposes `BN` only on its default export under Node's ESM loader, while bundlers expose a named export. `@noisedlabs/sdk` 0.9.0 includes the fix (`anchor.BN ?? anchor.default.BN`), so `buildSwapTx` on the bonding curve works under plain Node; earlier builds failed there with "BN is not a constructor" (the CHANGELOG lists the fix in its "renamed to Noised" entry).
- **`bigint: Failed to load bindings, pure JS will be used`.** `@solana/web3.js`'s `bigint-buffer` dependency prints this in Node when it has no native build (install scripts disabled). It is harmless.
- **Running the examples.** Node 22.18 and later run TypeScript files directly; on 22.12 to 22.17 add `--experimental-strip-types`.
- **Bundle size.** The SDK pulls in Meteora's DBC SDK (for swap quotes) and anchor. If you only need rules and graphs, import `@noisedlabs/sdk/programmable`, which has no Solana client dependency.

## Versioning and stability

- **0.x.** The SDK follows semantic versioning with the `0.x` rule: a **minor** release (0.9 to 0.10) may break the API; a patch release does not. Breaking changes are marked **BREAKING** in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/sdk/CHANGELOG.md), each with what to change.
- **Pin exactly.** Depend on an exact version, read the CHANGELOG before upgrading, and re-run `npm audit signatures` after every install.
- **The programs can change too.** They are upgradeable devnet deployments. The SDK targets the program builds of this repository (its IDLs are byte copies, and its tests check its layouts and constants against the programs' sources); the devnet programs run builds made before the rename to Noised, with the same instructions, accounts, errors and signature domains ([docs/DEVNET.md](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/DEVNET.md)). A program change that alters an interface ships with a new SDK version.
- **Frozen wire formats.** Signature domain tags, key derivations and the message formats the programs verify (attestation v3, authorization v1, withdrawal v4, metadata hash v2, PXR1, PXG1) are byte-stable: changing one would change every signature and every key derived from a phrase or passkey. The rename to Noised kept every domain tag (`phalanx/pq/...`, `PHX-...`).
- **Deprecations** are kept for a release where possible and marked `@deprecated` (for example `QslResult.components`, `pqIdentity.leafProbeStart`).

## API reference

Everything below is exported from the package root (`import { … } from "@noisedlabs/sdk"`); the other `exports` paths are `@noisedlabs/sdk/programmable` (the pure programmable module: [programmable launches reference](#programmable-launches-reference)), `@noisedlabs/sdk/idl/<name>.json` and `@noisedlabs/sdk/package.json`. Four modules are exported as namespaces: `lmots`, `lms`, `pqIdentity` and `leafLedger`. Signatures use `conn: Connection`, `PublicKey`, `Keypair` and `Transaction` from `@solana/web3.js`. The web app renders the generated reference of every export at [noised.fun/docs/sdk](https://noised.fun/docs/sdk).

### Constants

| Export | What |
|---|---|
| `PROGRAM_IDS` | `{ launchpad, hook, vault, shield, dbc, dammV2, autopilot }` (Meteora DBC and DAMM v2 included). The same on every cluster. |
| `WSOL_MINT`, `KNOWN_ACCOUNTS`, `DEFAULT_PUBKEY` | Wrapped SOL; Token-2022, SPL Token, ATA, system, compute budget, memo, instructions sysvar, Meteora authorities. |
| `CLUSTERS`, `type Cluster` | `"mainnet" \| "devnet" \| "localnet"` with the cluster byte of the PQ key derivations (0, 1, 2). |
| `GENESIS_HASHES` | `{ mainnet, devnet }` genesis hashes (`assertCluster`, `clusterOfGenesisHash`). |
| `POLICY`, `DBC`, `HOOK_BOUNDS` | The launchpad's bounds, mirrored from the program and checked against its sources by the tests: safety policy v3, open delay 60..=1,800 s, execution window 600 s, batch-cap floors (total cap ≥ threshold / 10, a non-zero wallet cap ≥ total cap / 200), at most 8 curve points, the attested launch window 60..=3,600 s opening at most 604,800 s ahead, metadata limits in UTF-8 bytes. |
| `SEEDS` | Every PDA seed (including `identity`, `attestation`, `payout-vault`, `metadata`, `rules`, and the autopilot's `autopilot`, `treasury`, `graph`, `auth`). |
| `PQ_IDENTITY` | LMS H10/W4 sizes (56-byte public key, 2,508-byte signature, 1,024 leaves, 128-byte bitmap `LEAF_BITMAP_LEN`), message tags (`"PHX-ATTEST-V3"`, 221-byte message with the rules hash; `"PHX-META-V2"`), account sizes (identity 196, attestation 2,708 (version 3, `ATTESTATION_OFFSETS`), payout vault 82), `attest_launch` v1 config words (300,000 CU, 2 MiB), the audit-round-4 limits (`CLOCK_SKEW_MAX_SECS`, `FREEZE_MAX_VALID_SECS`, `MAX_UNLANDED_SIGNATURES`). |
| `LAUNCH_RULES`, `HOOK_POLICY`, `AUTHORIZATION` | The creator rules record (`["rules", launch, rules_hash]`, `78 + len` bytes, at most 1,228 bytes of rules, `InvalidRules` 6048), the Launch Guard policy v2 (rules length at 275, bytes from 279), the post-quantum authorization (`"PHX-AUTH-V1"`, 140-byte message, 2,669-byte account, kinds 1 activate / 2 freeze / 3 revoke operator). |
| `METADATA` | The on-chain metadata record: seed `"metadata"`, name 1..=32, symbol 1..=10, uri at most 200 and document at most 3,072 UTF-8 bytes, `FLAG_INLINE_URI` 1 and `FLAG_EXTERNAL_URI` 2 (at most one), the uri prefixes (`"data:application/json;base64,"`, `"https://"`), `MAX_INLINE_URI_LEN` 4,125, the `TokenMeta` discriminator, offsets and size (`91 + strings`), `MINT_BASE_LEN` 386, the errors 6016 / 6045 / 6046 / 6047, the publish config words (100,000 CU, 2 MiB) and the document schema's limits (description 500 bytes, icon 64x64). |
| `PQ_VAULT_LAYOUT`, `VAULT` | How the launchpad recognizes a PQ vault; vault v4 (`"PHX-PQV4"`, 185-byte message, 2,176-byte signature, v1 config words). |
| `LAUNCH_GUARD`, `HOOK_ERRORS`, `CERTIFICATE`, `CERTIFICATE_CHECKS`, `CERTIFICATE_ALL_CHECKS`, `CERTIFICATE_RULES_BOUND`, `certificateChecksComplete(checks)` | The transfer-hook account layout and errors (6000..6012; 6010 `MutableOwner`, 6011 `RuleDenied`, 6012 `InvalidRules`); the certificate (version 4, 519 bytes, `metadata` at 455..487, `rules_hash` at 487..519; version 3, 487 bytes, is still read) and its twelve required bits (`PQ_ATTESTED` = 1024, `METADATA_ONCHAIN` = 2048; all = 4095) plus the informational `RULES_BOUND` = 4096 (a launch with creator rules has `checks` = 8,191). **Test `(checks & 4095) === 4095` (`certificateChecksComplete`), never `checks === 4095`.** |
| `MIGRATION_FEE_TIERS_BPS`, `DAMM_V2_MIGRATION_CONFIGS`, `TRUST_ANCHORS`, `FEE_PAYER_FUNDING_LAMPORTS` | Graduation fee tiers and configs; the reviewed Meteora and Token-2022 authorities and deploy slots; the default throwaway fee-payer funding (0.01 SOL). |
| `COMPUTE_UNITS`, `VAULT_COMPUTE_UNITS`, `ATTEST_COMPUTE_UNITS`, `AUTHORIZE_COMPUTE_UNITS`, `AUTOPILOT_COMPUTE_UNITS`, `PUBLISH_COMPUTE_UNITS`, `PUBLISH_RULES_COMPUTE_UNITS`, `MAX_COMPUTE_UNIT_LIMIT` | The builders' default compute-unit limits, measured per instruction; the runtime's ceiling (1,400,000). |
| `CLOCK_SKEW_MAX_SECS` (120n), `FREEZE_MAX_VALID_SECS` (86,400n), `GRAPH_TIMELOCK_SECS` (259,200n), `MAX_UNLANDED_SIGNATURES` (3), `MAX_BURN_ONLY_LANDINGS` (2), `KEEPER_OBSERVATION_WAIT_SECS` (60), `KEEPER_OBSERVER_INTERVAL_SECS` (600), `MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS` (5,000), `ATTEST_LANDING_MARGIN_SECS` (300n) | Limits used by the flows above. |
