### Launch

Parameters, policy and math:

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `PRESETS: Record<"fair" \| "community" \| "turbo", LaunchPreset>` | Frozen starting points (Fair: a 5-minute batch, a 6-hour guard, 1% max wallet, 0.5% max buy, 5 SOL per wallet in the batch; Community: 30 minutes, 24 hours, wallet-to-wallet transfers locked; Turbo: 1 minute, 1 hour, no per-wallet batch cap). Add `recipients` and `pqIdentity` (or use `planLaunch`). |
| `validateLaunchParams(p: LaunchParamsInput, forbidden?: PublicKey[]) → { ok, errors }` | Exact mirror of the program's policy, but reports every violation as `"field: message"`. `pqIdentity` must be 32 non-zero bytes. The token's metadata is not a launch parameter: it is a record checked by `validateTokenMeta` ([on-chain metadata](#on-chain-metadata-tokenmeta)). |
| `launchWindowIsValid(nowSecs, notBefore, notAfter)`, `launchWindowProblems(nowSecs, notBefore, notAfter)`, `inLaunchWindow(nowSecs, notBefore, notAfter)`, `validateLaunchWindow(notBefore, notAfter, { nowSecs, landingMarginSecs? })`, `defaultLaunchWindow(opensAt)` | The attested window, in bigint unix seconds. `launchWindowIsValid` is exactly the program's `pq::launch_window_is_valid` for an attestation landing at `nowSecs` (60..=3,600 s long, at least 60 s of it left when it lands: `max(nowSecs, notBefore) + 60 <= notAfter`, opening at most 7 days later), and `launchWindowProblems` explains it (empty exactly when valid). `inLaunchWindow`: `launch` runs only inside it, both ends inclusive. `validateLaunchWindow` checks before signing, allowing `landingMarginSecs` (default `ATTEST_LANDING_MARGIN_SECS`, 300 s) to land with 60 s of the window left. `defaultLaunchWindow`: `[opensAt, opensAt + 3,600]`. |
| `unixNowSecs(nowMs?)`, `clusterUnixTime(conn)`, `unixToIso(t)`, `unixToUtcText(t)`, `checkClockSkew(conn, { localNowSecs?, secondConnection?, maxClockSkewSecs? }) → ClockCheck` | "Now" as a bigint of unix seconds: the local clock, or the cluster's Clock sysvar (a clock that is not plausible unix seconds throws an error naming the RPC); absolute UTC dates; the clock comparison every signer of a time runs (`ClockSkewError`). |
| `launchParamsHash(p)` | The certificate's `params_hash` (`pqIdentity` included). The metadata hash the attestation signs is `metadataHashV2(record)`. |
| `serializeLaunchParams(p)`, `deserializeLaunchParams(data)` | Borsh `LaunchParams`, byte-identical to the program's. |
| `expectedBatchFill(launch, extraCommit?, existingCommit?) → BatchFill` | What the batch spends and refunds (pro rata above the total cap) and, for one commit, `spent`, `refund` and, once executed, `tokens`. Pass `extraCommit` only while the batch takes commits: once it executed, an extra commit throws a `RangeError`. |
| `launchPhase(launch, nowSecs: bigint)`, `batchOutcome(launch, nowSecs: bigint)` | `configured \| commit \| execute \| guarded \| open \| graduated`; `pending \| executed \| expired \| empty`. `launchPhase(launch, unixNowSecs())` for the local clock. |
| `designCurve(decimals, startPrice, graduationPrice, thresholdLamports)`, `estimateSupply(sqrtStartPrice, curve, threshold)`, `feeSummary(p)`, `splitFees(…)`, `batchShare(…)`, `proRata(…)` | Curve and fee arithmetic, as the programs compute it. |

Transaction builders (all also accept `ComputeBudgetOptions` in their last argument) and the recipient checks:

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `buildCreateLaunchTx(conn, creator, params: LaunchParamsInput, { launchSeed? }) → { tx, launch, launchSeed, warnings }` | `create_launch`. Refuses invalid parameters and fee recipients whose tokens nobody could ever move (`checkFeeRecipients`). Fee recipients are paid at ATA(wallet, wSOL), so a wSOL PQ vault is a valid (recommended) recipient, and a PQ vault of another mint is refused (it never releases wSOL, so its share would be lost). The creator signs. |
| `buildLaunchTx(conn, payer, launch, baseMint: Keypair, { nowSecs? }) → { tx }` | `launch` (no arguments: the mint's name, symbol and uri come from the record the attestation names, its 22nd account; the hook policy's creator rules from the rules record it names, the 23rd account, present exactly when the attested rules hash is not zero, else the launchpad program id; 988 bytes legacy without rules, 1,020 with, 300,000 CU): permissionless inside the attested window (any `payer`). Refuses a missing or empty attestation, a missing metadata or rules record and a time outside the window (cluster clock). Partially signed by the fresh mint keypair: add the payer's signature with `partialSign`. Inside the window the first `launch` to land wins. |
| `buildLaunchCommitBundleV1(conn, payer: Keypair, launch, baseMint: Keypair, lamports, { nowSecs?, refundOwner?, loadedAccountsDataSizeLimit? }) → { tx: Uint8Array, signature, blockhash, lastValidBlockHeight, computeUnitLimit, priorityFeeLamports }` | `[launch, commit]` as one signed v1 transaction (for keepers and scripts). |
| `buildCommitTx(conn, owner, launch, lamports, { tokenOwner?, refundOwner? }) → Transaction` | Wraps SOL and commits it. `tokenOwner` = the committer (default) or an opened PQ vault of the launch's mint; `refundOwner` = the committer or a wSOL PQ vault. Both are fixed by the owner's first commit. Commits for one vault are held to one wallet's cap together. |
| `buildExecuteBatchTx(conn, payer, launch) → Transaction` | `execute_batch` (permissionless keeper). Send it as a top-level instruction with a priority fee. |
| `buildClaimTx(conn, payer, launch, owner) → Transaction` | `claim` (permissionless): pays the commit's payout owners (tokens to ATA(token owner), the refund to ATA(refund owner)). There is no `claim_to`: the payout owners are fixed at the first commit. |
| `buildClaimFeesTx`, `buildClaimSurplusTx`, `buildDistributeTx` `(conn, payer, launch) → Transaction`; `buildClaimLpFeesTx(conn, payer, launch) → Transaction[]` | Fee collection and distribution (one transaction per LP position with fees). `findLaunchLpPositions`, `pendingPositionFees` read the positions. |
| `buildSwapTx(conn, user, mint, side: "buy" \| "sell", amountIn, slippageBps, { recipient?, computeUnitLimit?, computeUnitPrice? }) → { tx, quote, warnings }` | Swap on the bonding curve (Meteora DBC) or, after graduation, on the DAMM v2 pool. `recipient` sends the output to another owner's token account, e.g. a PQ vault. Refuses buys the Launch Guard would refuse (including, while the guard is on, a buy into a token account whose owner can be reassigned: `MutableOwner`, 6010); slippage at most 50%. The compute budget is opt-in and refused when the swap would no longer fit 1,232 bytes. |
| `checkTokenRecipient(conn, recipient, mint, tokenProgram, account?) → { ok, kind, refusals, warnings, ata }`, `checkFeeRecipients(conn, recipients, accounts?, { launch? }) → { ok, refusals, warnings }`, `checkGraphRecipients(conn, recipients) → { ok, refusals, warnings, withoutAccount }`, `isPqVaultOf(account, mint)`, `pqVaultMint(account)` | Whether paying ATA(recipient, mint) could strand the tokens; `checkFeeRecipients` is what `buildCreateLaunchTx` runs over the fee recipients (a wizard can run it as each one is entered). With `launch`, the launch's own autopilot treasury (`autopilotTreasuryAddress(launch)`) is accepted with a warning (only an autopilot graph its identity activates can spend it). `checkGraphRecipients` checks an autopilot graph's payees the same way. |

Creator rules on-chain (`publish_rules`): the rules (PXR1 bytes from `compileRules`) are a record at `["rules", launch, rules_hash]`, verified for the launch's guard when written, never modified or closed, and signed by the attestation (message v3); `launch` installs exactly those bytes in the hook policy. Publish them from the throwaway payer before the attestation and wait until they are final.

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `buildPublishRulesV1Tx(conn, payer: Keypair, { launch, rules, computeUnitPrice?, computeUnitLimit?, loadedAccountsDataSizeLimit? }) → PublishRulesV1Ready \| PublishRulesAlreadyPublished`, `sendPublishRulesTx(conn, built, { commitment? }) → LaunchRulesAccount`, `waitForLaunchRules(conn, launch, rulesHash, opts?)` | A signed v1 transaction from the throwaway payer (any rule set: 580 bytes for the typical 286-byte set, 1,522 for the largest, 1,228 bytes). Refuses rules that do not verify for the launch's guard (`InvalidRules` 6048), a missing or live launch (`WrongLaunchState`); idempotent (`already-published`). |
| `buildPublishRulesTx(conn, payer: PublicKey, { launch, rules, … }) → PublishRulesLegacyReady \| PublishRulesAlreadyPublished` | The same as an unsigned legacy transaction any wallet pays, up to `PUBLISH_RULES_LEGACY_MAX_BYTES` = 898 bytes of rules. |
| `publishRulesInstruction(payer, launch, bytes)`, `publishRulesLegacySize(len, { priorityFee? })`, `publishRulesV1Size(len, { priorityFee? })`, `publishRulesFeeLamports(opts?)`, `launchRulesRentDue(conn, launch, bytes)`, `launchRulesSpace(len)`, `isLaunchRulesRecord(account, launch, rulesHash)`, `launchRulesRecordExists(conn, launch, rulesHash, commitment?)` | Pure building blocks; `isLaunchRulesRecord` is exactly the program's test of a record (`pq::is_rules_record`): anything else at the address makes an attestation naming the hash burn-only. |

### Launch flow (PQ v2)

```text
prepareFeeVault → buildMetadataDoc → planLaunch → buildPlannedCreateLaunchTx (wallet signs) → wait until finalized
→ buildFundThrowawayPayerTx (wallet signs) → buildPlannedPublishTx + sendPublishMetadataTx (throwaway payer) → waitForTokenMeta (finalized)
→ [rules] buildPlannedPublishRulesTx + sendPublishRulesTx (throwaway payer) → waitForLaunchRules (finalized)
→ buildPlannedAttestTx (identity signs, throwaway payer) → sendAttestLaunchTx
→ [autopilot] planGraphActivation → buildNextGraphActivationTx … (identity approves)
→ buildSweepPayerTx → waitForLaunchWindow → buildPlannedLaunchTx (anyone) → buildCommitTx → buildExecuteBatchTx → buildClaimTx
```

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `planLaunch({ creator, identity, preset? \| params?, recipients? \| feeVault, metadata: { name, symbol, doc?, flags?, uri? }, rules?, opensAt, windowSecs?, launchSeed?, nowSecs? }) → LaunchPlan` | Pure. Validates like the program (the record exactly as `publish_metadata` does, the rules as `publish_rules` does for the plan's guard) and fixes the launch address, `paramsHash`, the record's exact bytes (`metadata`), its `metadataHash`, its address (`tokenMeta`), the uri the mint will get (`tokenUri`, empty by default), the creator rules (`rules`, `rulesHash`, `rulesRecord`, `rulesExplanation` in plain English; none by default), the window (`window`, `windowIso`) and the exact 221-byte `message` the identity will sign (`messageHash`). Fee recipients default to everything to `feeVault`. Keep the plan: later steps need its exact record and seed. |
| `buildPlannedCreateLaunchTx(conn, plan)`, `buildPlannedPublishTx(conn, plan, payer: Keypair, opts?)`, `buildPlannedPublishRulesTx(conn, plan, payer: Keypair, opts?)` (null without rules), `buildPlannedAttestTx(conn, plan, { identity, ledger, payer?, allowLocalnet?, landingMarginSecs?, metadataCommitment?, rulesCommitment?, maxBurnOnlyLandings?, acknowledgeExtraSignatures?, signingLock?, localNowSecs?, secondConnection?, maxClockSkewSecs? })`, `buildPlannedLaunchTx(conn, plan, payer, baseMint)`, `buildPlannedLaunchCommitBundle(conn, plan, payer, baseMint, lamports)` | The steps, with the plan's values. The attest step passes `plan.messageHash` as `expectedMessageHash`, and refuses a launch holding any configuration other than the planned one, and a metadata or rules record that is not published and final. |
| `replanLaunchWindow(plan, { opensAt, windowSecs?, nowSecs?, metadata? }) → LaunchPlan` | The window passed without a launch (`window-missed`): the same launch with a new window (and, with `metadata`, a new record to publish first). The identity signs its message at the next leaf, which replaces the unused attestation (audit round 3 F1). |
| `preparePqVault(conn, { master, cluster, mint, payer, account?, allowLocalnet? }) → { vault, mint, account, genesisKeyId, tokenAccount, opened, openTx }`, `prepareFeeVault(conn, {…})` (wSOL), `vaultFeeRecipients(vault)` | The phrase's vault for a mint and its `open_vault` transaction when it is not open. Only an opened vault can be a fee recipient or payout owner. |
| `getLaunchFlowStatus(conn, launch, { nowSecs?, expectedMessageHash?, expectedMetadataHash?, expectedRulesHash?, owner?, pending?: { ledger, lmsPublicKey } }) → LaunchFlowStatus` | `step`: `create`, `publish` (the record of `expectedMetadataHash`, or the rules of `expectedRulesHash`, are not published yet), `attest`, `wait-for-window`, `launch`, `window-missed` ("Window passed: sign a new opening time"), `commit`, `execute`, `claim` or `trading`, with a one-line `summary`, the attestation, the record (`tokenMeta`, `metadataPublished`, `rulesPublished`), the window (`window`, `windowIso`) and the seconds until it opens and closes. `warnings`: at `window-missed`, that an older signature that never landed can still take the slot; with `pending`, `pendingSignatures` (`findPendingAttestations`) and, while the attested window holds the slot, the advice to retire them now (`landOrBurnPending` with `burnOnly`). |
| `waitForLaunchWindow(conn, launch, { signal?, pollIntervalMs?, sleep? })` | Polls the cluster clock until the window opens. |

### Quick launch (planQuickLaunch)

`planQuickLaunch({ name, symbol, x?, website?, description?, iconPng, feeBps, feeDestination, creator, identity, launchSeed?, opensAt?, windowSecs?, nowSecs?, buyback? }) → QuickLaunchPlan` turns a short form into everything a launch needs, validated in one go (one `Error` listing every problem). Pure. See [quick launch, end to end](#quick-launch-end-to-end).

- `feeBps`: the trading fee (`QUICK_LAUNCH_FEE_BPS_RANGE`, 25 to 833 bps, so the fee plus its busy-market extra stays within the 10% ceiling); the rest of the parameters are the Fair preset's.
- `feeDestination`: `"wallet"` (all creator fees to `creator`), `"buyback-burn"` (all to the launch's autopilot treasury, `autopilotTreasuryAddress(launch)`, which a daily buyback-and-burn graph spends), or `{ split: walletBps }` (both). With the treasury, `graph` is the daily buyback-and-burn template with safe defaults (`QUICK_LAUNCH_BUYBACK_DEFAULTS`: 0.5 SOL per day, at most 3% above the recent low price, only with 0.5 SOL in the treasury; `buyback` overrides within `QUICK_LAUNCH_BUYBACK_RANGES`; a premium below the pool's fee is refused, since such a buyback could never fill).
- The plan: `launch`, `launchSeed`, `creator`, `params` (recipients and identity included), `recipients`, `treasury`, `metadata` (the record with its document: links and icon) and `metadataHash`, `launchInput` (pass it to `planLaunch` with the opening time), `plan` (the `LaunchPlan` when `opensAt` is given), `graph { template, bytes, hash, explanation, publishVia }`, `steps` (what the app runs, in order, each `{ id, title, detail, signer: "creator-wallet" \| "throwaway-payer" \| "anyone" \| "pq-identity", sdk, when }` in plain English), `summary` (plain-English lines for the creator) and `warnings`.

### On-chain metadata (`TokenMeta`)

A token's metadata is a record the launchpad stores whole, never modifies and never closes: `TokenMeta` at `["metadata", launch, metadata_hash]`, where `metadata_hash = metadataHashV2(record)` = `SHA256("PHX-META-V2" || u32le(len) name || u32le(len) symbol || u8 flags || u32le(len) uri || u32le(len) doc)` over UTF-8 bytes. The address is the content's hash, so nobody can put other bytes there. The identity signs that hash (attestation message v3, with the creator rules' hash), `attest_launch` attests only a record that exists, and `launch` gives the mint the record's name and symbol and the derived uri (empty by default). Anyone may publish other records under a launch: they are inert, so **resolve a token's record only through `Attestation.metadata_hash` (before launch) or `Certificate.metadata` (after), never by searching a launch's records.**

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `buildMetadataDoc({ name, symbol, description?, iconPng?, links?: { website?, x?, telegram? } }) → Uint8Array`, `validateMetadataDoc(input) → { ok, errors }` | The document: compact JSON, keys in the fixed order `name, symbol, description, image, external_url, extensions{x, telegram}`, empty parts left out, the icon as `data:image/png;base64,…` (a PNG of at most 64x64), `https://` links (X and Telegram to their own hosts), a description of at most 500 bytes, at most 3,072 bytes in all. The same input gives the same bytes. |
| `parseMetadataDoc(doc, { name?, symbol? }) → ParsedMetadataDoc { ok, empty, problems, warnings, name, symbol, description, icon: { png, dataUri, width, height } \| null, links: [{ kind, url, host }] }` | Reads a document without trusting it and without fetching anything: size cap, strict UTF-8, `JSON.parse`, an object; `image` only `data:image/png;base64,` (canonical base64) of a well-formed PNG of at most 64x64; links are inert text with their host spelled out (unusable ones dropped with a warning); a name or symbol other than the record's is a problem; a document not in the canonical form is a warning. Show a part only when it is not null. |
| `encodeIndexedPng(rgbaOrIndexed, width, height, maxColours = 16, { compression?: "auto" \| "store" }) → Promise<Uint8Array>`, `pngInfo(png)`, `crc32`, `PNG_SIGNATURE`, `PngError` | A small palette PNG for the icon (32x32 with 16 colours is about 130 to 700 bytes): RGBA quantized deterministically (or `{ indices, palette }` as given), the smallest bit depth, tRNS only when needed, IDAT through `CompressionStream("deflate")` when available and smaller, else stored. The same input gives the same bytes on one platform (`"store"`: on every platform); keep the bytes that were signed. `pngInfo` checks a PNG's structure (signature, CRCs, IHDR first, IEND last). |
| `validateTokenMeta(record) → { ok, error: { code, name } \| null, errors }` | The record exactly as `publish_metadata` checks it, in its order: flags (6045: at most one of `FLAG_INLINE_URI`, `FLAG_EXTERNAL_URI`), lengths (6046: document ≤ 3,072, uri ≤ 200 bytes), name 1..=32 and symbol 1..=10 bytes and an external uri of `https://` plus printable ASCII (6016), then a uri without `FLAG_EXTERNAL_URI` or an inline uri without a document (6045). `error` is what the program would answer. |
| `metadataHashV2(record)`, `tokenMetaRecord(record)`, `tokenMetaBorsh(record)`, `tokenMetaSpace(record)`, `externalUriIsValid(uri)`, `tokenUri(record)`, `tokenUriBytes(record)`, `launchedMintSpace(record)`, `tokenMetaAccountData(launch, record)` | The record's bytes, hash, account size (`91 + name + symbol + uri + doc`), the uri `launch` gives the mint (`""`, `"data:application/json;base64," + base64(doc)` or the external uri) and the mint's size (`386 + name + symbol + uri`). |
| `buildPublishMetadataTx(conn, { launch, payer: Keypair, metadata, computeUnitPrice?, computeUnitLimit?, loadedAccountsDataSizeLimit? }) → PublishMetadataTx` | Signed v1 bytes from the throwaway payer (`status: "ready"`, with `tx`, `signature`, `metadataHash`, `tokenMeta`, `rentLamports`, `fundingLamports`), or `already-published` (publishing is idempotent: the record is there, by anyone). Refuses, before signing, a record the program would refuse, a launch that does not exist or is already live, and a transaction over 4,096 bytes (309 to 3,621 bytes; 100,000 CU). |
| `sendPublishMetadataTx(conn, built, { commitment?, skipPreflight? }) → TokenMetaAccount`, `waitForTokenMeta(conn, launch, metadataHash, { commitment?, timeoutMs?, pollIntervalMs?, signal? })` | Send (refusing an underfunded payer or a remainder below the rent-exempt minimum first: `PublishPayerFundingError`); a send that fails while the record is there anyway (a racing copy) returns the record. Then wait until it is FINALIZED (the default) before the attestation. |
| `throwawayPayerFunding(conn, { metadata?, rules?, launch?, lmsPublicKey?, publish?, publishRules?, attest? }) → { lamports, tokenMetaRent, identityRent, attestationRent, publishFee, rulesRent, publishRulesFee, attestFee, rentFloor }`, `buildFundThrowawayPayerTx(conn, from, payer, { lamports?, …same options })`, `buildSweepPayerTx(conn, payer: Keypair, to) → { tx, lamports } \| null` | One total for the throwaway payer: the record's rent and the publish fee, the identity's and attestation's rents and the attest fee, rents read from the cluster (`getMinimumBalanceForRentExemption`), accounts that exist already not counted, plus the rent-exempt minimum when the payer would otherwise hold less than it between the two transactions. With `rules`, the rules record's rent and its publish fee too. The sweep returns what is left to the creator. |

Show a record from someone's token only after `verifyAttestation` or `verifyLaunch` verified it. |

### Post-quantum creator identity (LMS)

`pqIdentity` namespace (see [the post-quantum identity](#the-post-quantum-identity)):

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `importMaster(phrase) → PqMaster { entropy, master }`, `exportMasterAsPhrase(m)`, `wipeMaster(m)` | The 24 words and their 64-byte BIP-39 seed. `exportMasterAsPhrase` is the backup and is checked to restore the identical master. The words come from `generateRecoveryPhrase()` (package root). |
| `passkeyCreationOptions({ rpId, rpName, userName, userDisplayName?, userId?, challenge?, attachment?, excludeCredentialIds?, timeoutMs? })`, `passkeyRequestOptions({ rpId, credentialIds?, challenge?, timeoutMs? })`, `deriveMasterFromPasskeyAssertion(assertion, { rpId })`, `passkeyPrfFromAssertion(assertion, { rpId })`, `deriveMasterFromPasskeyPrf(prf, { userVerified: true })`, `passkeyEntropy(prf)`, `passkeyPrfSalt()`, `checkPasskeyRpId(rpId)` | The passkey path (WebAuthn PRF with user verification): `entropy = HKDF-SHA256(prf, "phalanx/pq/passkey/v1", "phalanx/pq/passkey/v1/bip39-entropy", 32)`, then the same master as the 24 words of that entropy. The RP ID is the exact app host. |
| `deriveIdentity(master, cluster, index, { cache?, onProgress?, signal?, expectedPublicKey? }) → PqIdentity { cluster, index, keyPair, publicKey, identityId, address }`, `deriveIdentityFromPhrase(phrase, cluster, index, opts?)`, `deriveIdentityKey(master, cluster, index)` | Key generation is non-blocking (time slices with progress, about 0.6 s in Node on a desktop CPU). With a tree cache, an identity loads in milliseconds. |
| `attestationMessage(fields)`, `parseAttestationMessage(msg)`, `authorizationMessage(fields)`, `parseAuthorizationMessage(msg)`, `MIN_LAUNCH_WINDOW_SECS`, `MAX_LAUNCH_WINDOW_SECS`, `MAX_LAUNCH_LEAD_SECS` | What the identity signs: the 221-byte message v3 (`"PHX-ATTEST-V3"`, launchpad, launch, `params_hash`, creator, `metadataHashV2` of the record, `rulesHash` of the creator rules (all zero: none), the window); and the 140-byte authorization (`"PHX-AUTH-V1"`, launchpad, launch, creator, kind, payload hash) of `pq_authorize`. The 189-byte v2 is retired: the program builds only v3, so a v2 signature never lands. A signature over an unpublished record or an invalid window lands only to burn its leaf: the checks to run before signing are the root's (`validateTokenMeta`, `validateLaunchWindow`, …). |
| `chooseLeaf(keyPair, message, used, taken?) → { leaf, probeStart, usedCount, warn, exhausted, unknownUsed, leafSetOnChain }`, `nextFreeLeaf(used, start, taken?)`, `leafUsed`, `markLeafUsed`, `usedLeafCount`, `usedLeaves`; `leafProbeStart(id, message)` (deprecated) | Leaf selection (audit round 4, ID-F1). The walk starts at the identity's **secret** probe (`keyPair.leafProbeStart(message)`: `HMAC-SHA256` under a key derived from the identity's seed, tag `"phalanx/pq/identity/leaf/v2"`), so nobody without the seed can predict a leaf, and it skips only leaves the ledger (or this process) holds: bits the RPC reports never move it. `unknownUsed` lists bits set on-chain the caller's records do not explain and `leafSetOnChain` says whether the chosen leaf is one of them; the signers refuse in either case (`UnknownLeavesError`). `leafProbeStart(id, message)` is the public probe of SDK 0.8 and older, kept for vectors only. |
| `attestationAttestsMessage(attestation, message)`, `decodePqAttestEvent(data)` | After landing: does the attestation hold this message? Events `LaunchAttested` (with `rulesHash`), `PqLeafConsumed`, `Authorized` and `RulesPublished`. |

`lms` namespace: `lmsVerify(publicKey, message, signature) → leaf | null` (RFC 8554 Algorithm 6a, exactly as the Rust crate), `lmsKeygen(sk, opts?)`, `lmsKeygenSync(sk)`, `lmsKeyPair(sk, { cache?, expectedPublicKey?, … })`, `lmsKeyPairFromTreeCache(sk, cache)`, `memoryTreeCacheStore()`, `treeCacheKey(sk)`, `parseLmsPublicKey`, `parseLmsSignature`, `encodeLmsPublicKey`, `identityId(publicKey)`, `secretLeafProbeStart`. `LmsKeyPair` has `publicKey`, `identityId`, `root`, `authPath(q)`, `randomizer(q, message)`, `leafProbeStart(message)` (the secret probe v2), `exportTreeCache()` (65,536 bytes, authenticated) and `wipe()`, and no signing method: an identity signs only through the leaf ledger (`reserveAndSign`, `signAtNextLeaf`, `buildAttestLaunchTx`), whose deterministic signatures are byte-identical to the Rust signer and verified before they are returned.

`leafLedger` namespace: the durable record of which leaf belongs to which message (see [the leaf ledger](#the-leaf-ledger)).

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `createLeafLedger(store: LeafLedgerStore, { lock? }) → LeafLedger` | `store` is `{ get, add, put, keys, singleRealmOnly? }` with an **atomic** `add` (write only if absent: IndexedDB `add()`, SQL `INSERT`, an exclusive file create). In a browser pass `lock: (name, fn) => navigator.locks.request(name, () => fn())` so tabs are serialized; a store atomic within one tab only (`singleRealmOnly`) is refused without it. Records written under the project's earlier name (`phalanx/pq/…`) are migrated and honoured (`migrateLegacyLedgerRecords`, package root). |
| `memoryLeafLedgerStore()`, `storageLeafLedgerStore(localStorage)`, `createMemoryLeafLedger()` | Stores for tests, or Web Storage (atomic within one tab only, so `createLeafLedger` requires the cross-tab lock; also call `navigator.storage.persist()`). |
| `exportLeafRecords(ledger, identityId) → LeafLedgerExport`, `importLeafRecords(ledger, publicKey, exported) → { added, merged, unchanged, conflicts, compromised }` | One identity on two devices: move the records before the second device signs. An import is authenticated (every signature re-verified, nothing written otherwise), only adds taken leaves, burns a local reservation that never signed at a leaf the other device signed, and reports leaves holding two signatures. A record without a signature proves nothing: it only marks its leaf taken (`burned`, no message) and never re-points a message that holds a live leaf (audit round 4, ID-F2b / ID-F3). |
| `acknowledgeUnknownLeaves(ledger, publicKey, used, { expectedCount }) → { added, burned }`, `UnknownLeavesError { identityId, unknownLeaves, unknownCount, usedOnChain, knownToLedger, chosenLeaf, chosenLeafSetOnChain }` | Audit round 4, ID-F1c (both also at the package root). The signers refuse, before anything is reserved, while the identity's bitmap shows leaves this ledger never signed at. Import the other device's records first. Only when the user confirms that every signature made elsewhere has landed, record those leaves as taken with `acknowledgeUnknownLeaves`, passing the count the user saw (`unknownCount`): a different count is refused. A very large count is a sign of a lying RPC: do not confirm it. |
| `signAtNextLeaf(ledger, keyPair, message, used, { launch? }) → { leaf, signature, selection }`, `reserveAndSign(ledger, keyPair, leaf, message)`, `selectLeaf(ledger, { keyPair, message, used })`, `pendingSignatures(ledger, identityId)`, `launchSignatures(ledger, identityId, launch)`, `holdsMessageLeaf(record)` | Reserve the leaf for the message, sign deterministically, record the signature, and only then return it. The same message always gets the same leaf and bytes. `reserveAndSign` refuses (`LeafLedgerError`) when the record the ledger returns is not this identity's reservation of that leaf for that message, and, in one process, a leaf that signed one message never signs another, whatever ledger is passed (`LeafConflictError`). `launchSignatures` lists every window the identity signed for a launch, read from the signed bytes. A custom `LeafLedger` must keep the contract of `createLeafLedger` (an atomic add; a record is never reassigned). |

### Attestation (`attest_launch`)

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `buildAttestLaunchTx(conn, { launch, creator, identity, ledger, metadataHash, rulesHash?, window: { notBefore, notAfter }, expectedParamsHash, payer?, allowLocalnet?, landingMarginSecs?, launchCommitment?, metadataCommitment?, rulesCommitment?, maxBurnOnlyLandings?, expectedMessageHash?, acknowledgeExtraSignatures?, signingLock?, localNowSecs?, secondConnection?, maxClockSkewSecs? }) → AttestLaunchTx` | `expectedParamsHash` (`launchParamsHash` of the reviewed parameters) is required: a forged creator wallet can create a launch at the same PDA with its own parameters and this identity copied in. Only `unsafeAcceptAnyParams: true` (tooling) replaces it. Before reserving a leaf or signing, it refuses: an RPC of another cluster; a launch that is not finalized, not `Configured`, not created by `creator`, naming another identity, or holding other parameters; a cluster clock more than 120 s from this device's (`ClockSkewError`); a window the program would not attest (at least 60 s of it left when it lands, judged on both clocks); a message other than `expectedMessageHash`; a launch attested by another message whose window has not passed; a record (or, with a non-zero `rulesHash`, a rules record) that is not published or not finalized; then, under the launch's signing lock (`signingLockName(launch)`; default an in-process mutex, in a browser `navigator.locks`): earlier signatures that can still land (`PendingAttestationError`), more than `MAX_UNLANDED_SIGNATURES` (3) that never landed (`SignatureCapError`, unless `acknowledgeExtraSignatures`), `maxBurnOnlyLandings` (default 2) burn-only landings (`AttestRetryLimitError`), and used leaves the ledger does not know (`UnknownLeavesError`). A rebuild of a recorded signature is never refused. `status`: `ready` (signed v1 `tx`, throwaway `payer`, `leaf`, `fundingLamports`, `windowIso`, …), `already-attested`, or `leaf-landed` (do not re-send; confirm). |
| `fundingLamportsForAttest(conn, { launch?, lmsPublicKey? })`, `attestRentLamports(conn, launch?, lmsPublicKey?)`, `attestFeeLamports(opts?)`, `buildFundAttestPayerTx(conn, from, payer, { lamports? }) → { tx, lamports }` | Funding of the attestation alone: rent of the accounts still missing + fee, read from the cluster. Fund the record and the attestation together with `throwawayPayerFunding`. |
| `sendAttestLaunchTx(conn, built, { ledger? }) → AttestationOutcome` | Refuses an underfunded payer before sending (`AttestPayerFundingError`), sends, then `confirmAttestation`. When the program refuses the accounts (ConstraintSeeds 2006: nothing written, the leaf not burned) it resends the SAME signature with the accounts derived again (`rewrapAttestTx`), never a new one; PqLeafUsed (6041) means this leaf already landed, and the outcome is read from the attestation. |
| `rewrapAttestTx(conn, built, opts?) → AttestLaunchReady` | The same LMS signature in a new transaction (fresh blockhash, accounts derived from what the signature names), keeping the priority fee the payer was funded for unless `opts` names another. Checks the signature still verifies at its leaf. |
| `confirmAttestation(conn, launch, expectedMessageHash, { leaf?, lmsPublicKey?, message?, ledger?, landedAt? })`, `burnReasons(input)` | `attested` only when the attestation holds this message's hash; `burned` (with `reasons`: `record-missing`, `rules-missing`, `invalid-window`, `wrong-identity`, `already-attested`) when the leaf was used without attesting; `pending` when nothing landed. Never assume a landing attested. |
| `attestationReplaceable(attestation, nowSecs)`, `AttestRetryLimitError`, `MAX_BURN_ONLY_LANDINGS` | Audit round 3 F1: an attestation is replaced only once its window passed unused (`nowSecs > notAfter`, the launch still `Configured`); the burn-only cap. |
| `findPendingAttestations(conn, { launch, lmsPublicKey, ledger, nowSecs?, localNowSecs? }) → PendingAttestation[]`, `PendingAttestationError { launch, pending }` | The launch's signatures the ledger holds that were never seen landing with a known outcome and whose window has not ended on both the cluster's clock and this device's, each with `window`, `windowIso`, `leaf`, `messageHash`, `leafSetOnChain` and `landingNow`: `attests` (it would take the slot and set the opening time to its window) or `burns`. |
| `landOrBurnPending(conn, { launch, identity, ledger, payer, burnOnly?, allowLocalnet? }) → { landings, remaining }`, `fundingLamportsForPending(conn, { launch, identity, ledger, count? })` | Re-sends the pending signatures with their recorded bytes (never a new signature), from a funded throwaway `payer`: each attests or only burns its leaf, and the ledger records it. Burns are marked `retired` and do not count against `maxBurnOnlyLandings`. With `burnOnly: true` only those that would just burn their leaf are landed: run it while the launch's attestation holds the slot. After the window passed, without `burnOnly`, those that only burn land first, then the newest that can attest. |
| `attestLaunchInstruction(args)` (7 accounts, `rulesHash` optional), `rulesAccountFor(launch, rulesHash)`, `signAttestTransaction(payer, ix, blockhash, opts?)`, `attestTransactionSize({ priorityFee?, rules? })`, `attestTxConfig(opts?)` | Pure building blocks (3,005 bytes without rules, 3,037 with, plus 8 with a priority fee, for every record and rule set). |

### Post-quantum vault (LM-OTS)

See [PQ vault: post-quantum custody](#pq-vault-post-quantum-custody).

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `generateRecoveryPhrase()`, `masterFromPhrase(phrase)`, `phraseProblems(phrase)`, `masterFingerprint(master)`, `normalizePhrase(phrase)`, `isBip39Word(word)` | A separate 24-word phrase; `master` is its BIP-39 seed (an all-zero master, i.e. a wiped buffer, is refused everywhere). |
| `deriveVaultKey(master, cluster, mint, account, sequence) → { skSeed, pk, keyId }`, `GENESIS_KEY_INDEX`, `nextKeyIndex(sequence)`, `keySequence(sequence)` | The key that signs at a vault's `sequence` is that sequence; the next key is `sequence + 1` (the program refuses any other: `InvalidKeyIndex`). |
| `checkVaultMint(conn, mint)`, `buildOpenVaultTx(conn, payer, mint, genesisPk)`, `buildDepositTx(conn, owner, mint, vault, amount)` | Open and fund a vault. Deposits go to the vault's token account; **SOL or another mint sent to the vault address itself is unrecoverable.** |
| `fetchVault(conn, vault) → VaultInfo`, `scanVaults(conn, master, cluster, mint, maxAccount)`, `listPayouts(conn, vault)`, `fetchPayout(conn, vault, sequence)` | State: `sequence`, current key, `balance`, `reserved`, `available`, unreleased payouts. |
| `checkRecipient(conn, destinationOwner, mint, vault, { wallet? }) → RecipientCheck { ok, refusals, recipientWarnings, mintWarnings, offCurveConfirmation, canonicalAta, destinationOwner, mint, vault, wallet }` | Run before signing and show the result. Never sign while `refusals` is not empty; the recipient warnings, the mint warnings and the off-curve case need three separate confirmations from the user. The result names the recipient, mint, vault and wallet it was made for. |
| `RecipientConfirmation { recipient: RecipientCheck, acknowledged: { recipientWarnings?, mintWarnings?, offCurveConfirmation? } }`, `RecipientConfirmationError { reason, current }` | What every vault signer requires as `opts.confirm`: `checkRecipient`'s result for this exact recipient, mint and vault, and the user's acknowledgment of each kind of caution it holds (`true` exactly where the check has one; `acknowledged: {}` when it has none). Refused before any signature or ledger write (`reason`): `missing`; `mismatch`; `refused`; `unacknowledged`; `stale` (show `current` and ask again). |
| `createVaultKeyLedger(store: LeafLedgerStore, { lock? }) → VaultKeyLedger`, `createMemoryVaultKeyLedger()`, `VaultKeyInUseError { record, withdrawal }`, `VaultLedgerError`, `withdrawalFromRecord(record)` | The durable one-signature-per-key record every vault signing call requires (same store interface and atomicity rule as the leaf ledger; one store can hold both). Each record holds its one-time key, and every signature recorded is verified under it. A key reserved or signed for one withdrawal never signs another, in any tab or device sharing the ledger. |
| `exportVaultKeyRecords(ledger, { vault? }) → VaultKeyLedgerExport { format, records, skipped }`, `importVaultKeyRecords(ledger, exported) → { added, merged, unchanged, conflicts, compromised, unverifiable }` | Several devices holding one phrase: export the signed records on the device that signed, import them on the other one BEFORE it signs. An import is authenticated and only adds; it reports keys given to two withdrawals (`conflicts`), keys holding two signatures (`compromised`: broadcast one of the two at once) and keys the other device signed with but could not export (`unverifiable`: do not sign here while it is not empty). |
| `completeVaultKeyRecords(ledger, master, cluster, mint, maxAccount) → { completed, remaining }` | Gives the records of SDK 0.2.0 (no key) of this phrase's vault accounts `0..=maxAccount` their key, re-derived and authenticated, so that they can be exported; nothing is signed. |

Throws `IncompleteSearchError` when it cannot rule out a revealed signature: pass `error.search.continuation` as `continueFrom` and call again. |
| `findPendingWithdrawal(conn, vault, { maxTransactions?, maxSignaturePages?, continueFrom? })`, `recordPendingWithdrawal(ledger, search) → WithdrawTxArgs` | The history search on its own (`complete`, `incompleteReason`, `continuation`, `pending`, `all`). Failed transactions that name the vault but not the current payout account (anyone can land those for the base fee) are read last, so a genuine attempt is found first. |
| `withdrawMessage(vault, mint, sequence, destinationOwner, maxAmount, nextKeyId)`, `signWithdrawal(conn, cluster, key, nextKey, msg, { ledger, confirm, allowLocalnet? })`, `parseWithdrawMessage(msg)` | The 185-byte message and the low-level signer (the same checks, on private copies; refuses when `key.skSeed` changes meanwhile). Prefer `prepareWithdrawal`. |

The fallback builder simulates (reveals) only a signature `ledger` holds for this exact withdrawal. Send only if `simulation.ok`. Rebuild from the recorded signature as often as needed. |

`lmots` namespace: RFC 8554 `LMOTS_SHA256_N32_W4` without a signer (`publicKey`, `keyId`, `verify`, `candidatePublicKey`, `randomizer`, `hmacSha256` and the sizes), as in the Rust crate `noised-lmots`. A vault key signs only through `prepareWithdrawal` / `signWithdrawal`.

### QSL-1 (`checkQsl1`, `qslBadge`)

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `checkQsl1(conn, mint, { commitment?, activateAt?, freezeNotAfter?, … }) → QslResult` | The verification algorithm of [QSL-1](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/docs/standard/QSL-1.md) §7: the genesis hash, then two `getMultipleAccounts` (step 1: the mint, the certificate, the hook policy and account list, the Noised, Meteora and Token-2022 programs; step 3: the launch, the DBC config and pool, the attestation, the identity, the record, the autopilot and, with rules, the rules record), one more read when an autopilot runs a graph and, after migration, `getTokenAccountsByOwner` of the launch authority with its positions and their pools; at `commitment` (default `finalized`), each read no older than the one before. Never `getProgramAccounts`, never a URL. Throws only when the RPC fails. |
| `QslResult { standard: "QSL-1", mint, slot, cluster, level: 0 \| 1 \| 2, candidate, wouldBe, programmable, graduated, migrated, checks, reasons, blocking, info, trusted, uriMode, certificateVersion }` | `level`: what is awarded (0 unless every condition holds on mainnet with finalized programs). `candidate`: every condition of `wouldBe` holds except program finality (C1.24) and/or the cluster. `checks`: every condition in order (`cluster`, C1.1..C1.24, C2.1..C2.8), each `{ id, level, title, status: "pass" \| "fail" \| "warn" \| "skip", ok, plain, detail }`. `reasons` / `blocking`: why the next level is not reached. `info`: §6.6's informational checks. `trusted`: §8.2's parties with their live upgrade authorities. `certificateVersion`: versions 3 and 4 are known, any other fails closed. C1.3 tests `(checks & 4095) == 4095` (8,191 with rules). `programmable: QslProgrammable { present, verified, rules?, autopilot?, checks, warnings }` describes the creator's launch rules and automation (§6.4), never a level: `checks` P.R1..P.R4, P.G1..P.G5, and `warnings` (`QslWarning { kind, component, plain, rule?, from?, to?, wallets? }`, most serious first: `insiderBuying`, `buysBlocked`, `rulesUnconfirmed`, `autopilotUnconfirmed`, `transferLimits`, `operator`, `updateQueued`, `longRule`, `notFrozen`, `autopilotUpgradeable`, `noOpRule`, `complexRule`). A component that fails its checks never lowers the level, and one that passes never raises it. Deprecated 0.7 aliases: `components { rules, autopilot }`. |
| `evaluateQsl1({ mint, genesisHash, slot, accounts, launchAuthorityTokenAccounts }, { activateAt?, activateAtSearchCap?, freezeNotAfter?, freezeNotAfterSearchCap? }) → QslResult`, `findActivateAt`, `findFreezeNotAfter` | The same evaluation, pure, on accounts already read (an indexer's cache). |
| `qslBadge(result) → QslBadge { label, name, title, tone, summary, lines, required, showOnTradeScreen, mint, programmable }` | QSL-1 Appendix A: `label` `"QSL-1 L1"`, `"QSL-1 L2"`, `"QSL-1 candidate"` or `"Not QSL-1"`; `title` the badge text; `programmable` the tag shown next to it when rules or automation are present (`{ tag: "programmable", text, link: "read its rules", summary, explain, warnings, tone }`, null otherwise; it never changes the label, title or tone); `tone` `positive`, `caution` or `neutral`; `lines` the one-line description, what it may also say and the `required` lines; `showOnTradeScreen` false for a candidate unless the cluster is known not to be mainnet. `QSL1_LEVEL_NAMES`, `QSL1_CONDITION_IDS`, `QSL1_PROGRAMMABLE_CHECK_IDS`. |

### Verify

`verifyLaunch(conn, mint, { nowSecs?: bigint, listOperators? }) → VerificationReport { mint, overall, phase, checks, trustedParties, certificate, pqOrigin, metadata, rules }`

The certificate is never trusted on its own: each check is recomputed from live accounts. Without `nowSecs` the phase is judged on the RPC's Clock sysvar; a clock that is not plausible unix seconds is reported (`rpc.clock`, a warning) and this device's clock is used instead. `listOperators` (default true) lists DAMM v2 operator accounts with `getProgramAccounts`.

- **Mint**: Token-2022, no mint or freeze authority, exactly the metadata pointer, metadata and transfer-hook extensions (two independent parsers must agree), immutable metadata, the Launch Guard hook while the curve runs and no hook afterwards.
- **Post-quantum origin** (`pq.origin`, `report.pqOrigin`): the attestation's LMS signature is re-verified against the identity account's public key, over the 221-byte message v3 **rebuilt from on-chain data** (the launch, its parameters hash and creator, the hash recomputed from the metadata record itself, the attested rules hash, and the window), at a leaf the identity's bitmap marks used; the certificate and launch must name the same identity, leaf, slot and record, and the launch must have gone live inside the window.
- **On-chain metadata** (`report.metadata: { address, record, document, verified }`): `metadata.onchain`, `metadata.match` and `metadata.icon`. The document is read with `parseMetadataDoc`; nothing is ever fetched. Show the icon, description and links only when `metadata.verified` is true.
- **Creator rules** (`launch.rules`, `report.rules: { hash, address, bytes, explanation, boundInPolicy, verified } | null`): the certificate's rules hash is the attested one, the hook policy holds exactly the attested rules record's bytes (none for the zero hash), `RULES_BOUND` is set exactly when there are rules (version 4), and the rules are valid for the launch's guard. Also **launch vs certificate**, the **batch** (caps, pro-rata accounting, first swap), the **snipe-shield end**, the graduated pool's **fee** (including the default dynamic fee), and the **upgrade authorities** of every program involved.

`trustedParties` lists who can still change the outcome (Meteora's upgrade multisig and operators, the Token-2022 multisig, validators, your RPC and wallet). Before launch, `verifyAttestation(conn, launch) → { verified, problems, launch, origin, tokenMeta, launchRules }` re-verifies an attestation, its identity, its record, its rules and its LMS signature from live accounts. Lower-level: `checkPqOrigin(inputs)` (pure), `explainLaunchRules(bytes, launch)`, `tokenMetadataFields(extension)`, `compareDammPoolFee(pool, migrationFeeOption)` and DAMM v2's fee arithmetic (`dammMaxFeeNumerator`, …), `TRUSTED_PARTIES`.

### Shield

`shieldAddresses(baseMint, baseTokenProgram?) → { shield, authority, zMint, escrow }`, `fetchShield(conn, baseMint)`, `decodeShield(address, data)`, `buildCreateShieldTx(conn, payer, baseMint)`, `buildWrapTx(conn, owner, baseMint, amount)`, `buildUnwrapTx(conn, owner, baseMint, amount)`, `shieldMintPolicy(account)`, `SHIELD_ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS`. Deployed on mainnet, not on devnet; it hides amounts, not parties, and its encryption is not post-quantum ([guide](#shield-private-balances)).

| Function | Notes |
|---|---|
| `simulateAndExplain(conn, tx: Transaction \| Uint8Array, commitment?) → SimulationReport` | Unsigned simulation of a legacy transaction or v1 bytes: `ok`, `error` (program errors of the launchpad, hook, vault, autopilot, shield, Meteora, Anchor and SPL Token mapped to names and messages), `errorCode`, `failedInstruction`, `logs`, `unitsConsumed`, `programs`, `unknownPrograms`, `signers`, `writableAccounts`, `feeLamports`, `sizeBytes` vs `sizeLimit`, `format`. |
| `sendAndConfirm(conn, tx, { lastValidBlockHeight?, skipPreflight?, commitment?, preflightCommitment? }) → signature` | Sends a fully signed legacy transaction or v1 bytes and waits for `commitment` (default `confirmed`; `finalized` works too); throws if it failed or expired. The preflight and the default expiry height use `preflightCommitment` (default `confirmed`, where the builders' blockhash is known). |
| `assertCluster(conn, cluster, { allowLocalnet? })`, `clusterOfGenesisHash(hash)`, `GENESIS_HASHES`, `ClusterMismatchError` | The genesis-hash check every PQ signing function runs. |
| `computeBudgetInstructions(opts, defaultLimit)`, `priorityFeeLamports(price, limit)`, `simulateComputeUnits(conn, tx)` | Compute budget: `simulateComputeUnits` returns units used + 10% for a transaction built with `computeUnitLimit: MAX_COMPUTE_UNIT_LIMIT`. |
| `compileV1Message`, `signV1Message`, `decodeV1Transaction`, `verifyV1Signatures`, `v1TransactionId`, `V1_MAX_TRANSACTION_SIZE`, `LEGACY_MAX_TRANSACTION_SIZE` | The v1 transaction format (SIMD-0385, up to 4,096 bytes); the legacy limit (1,232). |
| `explainProgramError(programId: string, code)`, `plainErrorMessage(programId, code)`, `PLAIN_ERROR_MESSAGES`, `customErrorCode(error)`, `explainTransactionError(err, logs)`, `failedInstructionIndex(err)`, `programLabel(programId)` | [Program errors](#program-errors). |
| `getSolBalance`, `getTokenBalance(conn, owner, mint)`, `getTokenSupply`, `getMintInfo`, `rentExemptLamports(conn, size)` | Helpers (bigint results). |

### Tokens and codecs

`parseMint(owner, data)`, `parseTokenAccount(owner, data)`, `tokenAccountExtensions(data)`, `hasImmutableOwner(data)`, `tokenMetadataOf(mint)`, `transferHookOf(mint)`, `ExtensionType`, `MintParseError` (strict Token-2022 parsers that refuse unknown extensions); `noisedHookAccounts(mint)` (the Launch Guard's four extra accounts in the launchpad's order), `resolveHookAccounts(conn, mint, parsed, transfers)` and `launchGuardEndTs(conn, mint, parsed)` (when the guard ends; null without Noised's hook); `IDLS`, `idlCodecs()` and `IdlCodec` (the IDL-driven borsh codec every builder uses).

## Programmable launches reference

Two small byte formats a creator can add to a launch, both verified on chain by `crates/noised-rules`:

- **Launch rules (PXR1)** add restrictions to the Launch Guard while it is on (see [custom launch with launch rules](#custom-launch-with-launch-rules)).
- **Autopilot graphs (PXG1)** run a launched token's treasury inside fixed on-chain bounds (see [autopilot](#autopilot-treasury-automation)).

Status: the launchpad, hook and autopilot are deployed on mainnet (protocol not initialized yet, so no launch exists there) and on devnet (older builds), upgradeable and not independently audited (see [status](#status)). Since 0.7.0 the launch rules are bound on-chain (`publish_rules`, attestation message v3, the hook policy and certificate v4), and the launchpad's post-quantum authorization (`pq_authorize`) drives the autopilot's `activate`, `freeze` and `revoke_operator`. Since 0.8.0 a freeze approval expires (`not_after`), the hook skips creator rules for holders' moves through the Noised vault or shield, and rules and automation are a description in QSL-1 ("programmable"), never a level. Since 0.9.0 the autopilot account is 1,244 bytes (it records the running graph's approval, `active_auth`, and keepers' partial buybacks), a keeper may buy back less than a step's cap when the pool cannot fill it, a distribution skips recipients without a wSOL account, and removing the operator names the running graph's approval (revoke payload v3).

The pure part is also its own entry point, without the Solana client stack: `import { … } from "@noisedlabs/sdk/programmable"` (everything below except the account readers and builders, which come from the root). Its own guide, with the text grammars of both languages: [`sdk/src/programmable/README.md`](https://github.com/NoisedLabs/noised/blob/main/sdk/src/programmable/README.md).

| Area | Exports |
|---|---|
| Rules | `rules()` builder (`key`, `deny`, `capAmount`, `capBalance`, `compile`, `hash`, `explain`, `toText`), `when` / `all` / `any` / `not` conditions, `compileRules`, `decompileRules`, `verifyRules`, `rulesHash`, `rulesHashHex`, `parseRules` / `tryParseRules` / `printRules` (text), `explainRules` (plain English, addresses in full), `simulateTransfer` (the hook's decision in its order: the built-in guard with `builtin`, `MutableOwner` for a destination without ImmutableOwner (`toImmutableOwner: false`), creator rules skipped when the program is the Noised vault or shield), `ruleWarnings` (what a holder should be warned about: insider-only buying and for how long, buys refused, wallet-to-wallet limits, rules on for more than an hour, rules that do nothing), `RULE_TEMPLATES` / `ruleTemplate` (`fair-start`, `anti-bot` (a limit of at least `MIN_TX_IX_COUNT_THRESHOLD` = 10 instructions), `whale-cap`, `team-cant-buy`; pass the launch's `guardSecs` and `openDelaySecs`), `mergeRuleSets`, `tradingWindow`. |
| Graphs | `graph()` builder (`operator`, `recipient`, `node`, `build`, `compile`, `hash`, `explain`, `toText`, `toCanvas`; triggers `every`, `after`, `onGraduation`, `whenever`; actions `buybackBurn`, `burn`, `distributeSol`), `compileGraph`, `decompileGraph`, `verifyGraph`, `graphHash`, `graphHashHex`, `parseGraph` / `tryParseGraph` / `printGraph`, the canvas model (`graphToCanvas`, `canvasToGraph`, `compileCanvas`, `decompileCanvas`, `autoLayout`, …), `explainGraph`, `GRAPH_TEMPLATES` / `graphTemplate` (`daily-buyback-burn`, `burn-on-graduation`, `revenue-share`, `ai-buyback`). |
| The program's decisions | `planRun` (the program's `plan_run`: due, condition across the reference and the observed prices (`conditionPrices`, `observedPrices`, `graphConditionOver`, `evalConditionBounded`), operator, observations, premium, minimum out, amount), `runAmount`, `recordRunRaw`, `takeTipRaw`, `checkActivation`, `checkFresh`, `checkApply`, `AUTOPILOT_ERRORS`; the price bounds `recordObservation`, `observationWindow`, `followReference`, `buybackCap`, `withinPremium`, `buybackMinOut`, `lowestObserved`; the payloads the creator's key signs, `activationPayload(autopilot, graphHash, activateAt)`, `freezePayload(autopilot, graphHash, notAfter)` (`"PHX-GRAPH-FRZ-V2"`), `checkFreezeWindow`, `revokePayload(autopilot, graphHash, operator, activeAuth)` (`"PHX-OP-REVOKE-V3"`); partial buybacks: `planPartial`, `planMaxTip`, `planValue(plan, burnPrice, kept?)`, `burnPrice`. Checked against vectors the program's own Rust functions wrote. |
| Keepers and simulation | `newAutopilotState(g, migrationSqrtPrice)`, `nodeStatus` / `nodeStatuses` / `findDueNodes` (with `poolFeeBps` and `poolSol`: whether the swap fills, and the amount to run with), `observePrice` (`update_price`), `simulateGraph` (requires `migrationPrice`, `poolFeeBps`, `poolSol`; returns `steps`, `totals`, `final`, `assumptions`), the swap estimate `estimateBuybackOut`, `premiumCoversFee`, `minPremiumForFee`. |
| Errors | `ProgError { code, at }`, `DslError { line, col, offset, length, hint, pretty }`, `VERIFY_ERRORS`, `isVerifyErrorCode`. |
| On chain (root only) | `autopilotAddress`, `autopilotTreasuryAddress`, `graphRecordAddress`, `authorizationAddress`, `autopilotPdas`; `decodeAutopilot`, `decodeGraphRecord`, `fetchAutopilot`, `fetchGraph`, `fetchGraphBytes`, `fetchAutopilotView`, `autopilotStateOf`, `fetchDueNodes` (the keeper's view); `buildInitAutopilotTx`, `buildBindMintTx`, `buildBindPoolTx`, `buildPublishGraphTx` (legacy, up to 898 bytes) / `buildPublishGraphV1Tx` (any graph), `buildApplyPendingTx`, `buildUpdatePriceTx`, `buildRunTx(conn, caller, launch, node, { amount?, operator?, tipAccount? })` (`skippedRecipients`, `costs`: it never creates a recipient's account, only the caller's own tip account; a distribution nobody can receive is refused, `NoRecipientAccount` 6042), `buildCreateRunAccountsTx(conn, payer, launch, { recipients? })`, `AUTOPILOT_COMPUTE_UNITS`; `decodeAutopilotEvent` (`NodeRan` with `partial`, `skipped`, `kept`, `paid`, `skippedRecipients`), `activeActivation(account)`, `checkGraphRecipients(conn, recipients)`. |
| Authorizations (root only) | `buildPqAuthorizeTx(conn, { launch, creator, identity, ledger, kind: 1 \| 2 \| 3, payloadHash, freezeNotAfter?, payer?, allowLocalnet?, acknowledgeExtraSignatures?, signingLock?, localNowSecs?, secondConnection?, maxClockSkewSecs?, … }) → ready \| already-authorized \| leaf-landed`: the launch's post-quantum identity signs `"PHX-AUTH-V1" \|\| launchpad \|\| launch \|\| creator \|\| kind \|\| payloadHash` (140 bytes) at a leaf the leaf ledger reserves first (the same bitmap and ledger as attestations), after the cluster, the launch (finalized, this creator, this identity), the clocks (kinds 1 and 2) and the kind are checked; a freeze needs `freezeNotAfter` and is refused once the cluster's clock is past it; a v1 transaction from a throwaway payer. `sendPqAuthorizeTx` (`AuthorizePayerFundingError`), `confirmAuthorization` (`authorized` / `burned` / `pending`), `rewrapPqAuthorizeTx`, `fundingLamportsForAuthorize`, `authorizeTransactionSize`, `pqAuthorizeInstruction`, `verifyAuthorization(auth, { launch, identity, expectedKind?, expectedPayloadHash? })`. |
| Graph changes (root only) | `buildActivateTx(conn, payer, launch, { graphHash, activateAt })`, `buildFreezeTx(conn, payer, launch, { notAfter })`, `buildRevokeOperatorTx(conn, payer, launch)` consume the `Authorization` (refusing what the program would: a stale or missing authorization, a replacement inside the 72-hour timelock, a frozen graph, an expired freeze (`FreezeExpired`, 6040), no operator); `planFreeze(conn, launch, { notAfter?, validForSecs? })` (default: one hour from the cluster's clock, `FREEZE_DEFAULT_VALID_SECS`; at most 24 hours after this device's clock, `FREEZE_MAX_VALID_SECS`), `getFreezeStatus`, `buildNextFreezeTx` (authorize, then freeze; never signs or lands after `not_after`); `planRevokeOperator(conn, launch)`; `planGraphActivation(conn, launch, graphBytes, { activateAt?, marginSecs?, … })` (a first graph may start at once, a replacement 72 hours later: `GRAPH_TIMELOCK_SECS`; payees checked; `activateAtIso`), `getGraphActivationStatus(conn, launch, plan)`, `buildNextGraphActivationTx(conn, launch, plan, { payer, throwaway?, identity?, ledger?, creator?, … })`. The plans refuse a cluster clock more than 120 s from this device's. |
| Keepers (root only) | `planKeeperStep(conn, caller, launch, { ownObservationAt?, poolFeeBps?, now?, computeUnitPrice? }) → apply-pending \| update-price (then wait `KEEPER_OBSERVATION_WAIT_SECS` = 60 s; `because`) \| wait \| run \| idle`, `runKeeper(conn, { caller, launch, send?, sleep?, maxSteps?, poolFeeBps? }) → { steps, signatures, stopped, detail, error, costLamports }`: a buyback runs only a minute after the keeper's OWN price check (`KEEPER_OBSERVER_INTERVAL_SECS` = 600 between independent checks), each step states its `costs` and a run its `expectedTipLamports`; a keeper never pays for a recipient's account. |
